How to access OneDrive settings

Applies to: SharePoint in Microsoft 365, OneDrive for Windows.

Use OneDrive settings to manage your accounts, backup, notifications, and sync preferences. Available settings vary by app and account type. Choose the tab for your OneDrive app.

Note

If you sign in with a work or school account, some settings might not be available. Contact your IT admin for help.

Windows

How to access OneDrive settings in Windows
  • Select the blue or white OneDrive cloud icon in the Windows taskbar notification area.
  • Tip
    • If the icon is hidden, select the Show hidden icons arrow next to the notification area.
    • If OneDrive isn’t running, select Start, enter OneDrive in the search box, and select OneDrive in the search results.
    • If you still don’t see the icon, see I can’t see any OneDrive icons.
  • Select Help & Settings (the gear icon ), and then select Settings. OneDrive settings opens. If you have both a personal account and a work or school account, open the cloud icon for the account you want to manage. Each account has its own settings.

The settings window shows your storage usage and includes Manage storage.

Sync and back up
  • Back up important PC folders to OneDrive. Your PC’s Desktop, Documents, and Pictures folders might not be automatically included in OneDrive. Select Manage back up to choose folders. For prerequisites and the effects of changing folder backup, see Back up your folders with OneDrive.
  • OneDrive personal users can also include Photos and videos and Screenshots folders in their OneDrive collection.
  • Use Preferences to choose how OneDrive behaves at startup, when your device is in battery saver mode, or when you’re connected to a metered network (hotspot).
  • Advanced settings include:
    • File collaboration which controls the sync direction of your files and enables you to work on files with other people at the same time. To ensure AutoSave works best, keep this turned on.
    • Adjust the Upload and Download rates to limit the bandwidth OneDrive uses. For work or school accounts, your IT admin might set these limits.
    • Files On-Demand helps you save space on your computer. See Save disk space with OneDrive Files On-Demand for Windows.
Account settings in Windows
  • You can Unlink or Add another account but you can only have one personal account active on each computer.
  • Select Choose folders to choose which OneDrive folders sync to your computer. For details and the effects of clearing a folder, see Choose which OneDrive folders to sync to your computer.
  • Change your Personal Vault auto-lock time.
Notifications
  • Turn on or turn off Notifications for some events.
About OneDrive in Windows
  • OneDrive info includes your device ID and version number. No personal information is shown here. Quoting your unique OneDrive Device ID when contacting support helps support agents assist you more efficiently. Selecting the version number shows you the OneDrive release notes.
  • OneDrive Insider program offers you a chance to get prerelease versions of OneDrive.
Other OneDrive options in Windows

For pause, resume, close, and recycle bin options, see Other OneDrive desktop options.

iPhone and iPad

How to access OneDrive settings on your Android or iOS device

To open the OneDrive mobile app settings:

  • Tap your profile picture or the profile icon .

  • Tap Settings. The mobile app settings include:

  • Accounts: Manage accounts. You can have only one personal account active.

  • Options: Manage camera roll, notifications, device security, and Personal Vault settings.

  • About: Find links to more support articles.

Web

How to access OneDrive settings on the OneDrive website

Sign in to OneDrive on the web to use the following settings links. These links open settings for a personal Microsoft account; work or school settings can differ.

  • Manage storage shows how much storage you’ve used and what plans and bonuses you have.
  • Plans and upgrades shows a summary of your existing storage plan or subscription.
  • Office File formats lets you choose the default file format for Office documents you create.
  • Personal Vault is where you manage how you sign in to your Personal Vault. When signed in, you can add or remove ways to get security codes.
  • Photos offers a toggle for automatically creating albums from photos you upload to the web. This feature isn’t the same as albums from your mobile camera roll.
  • Tagging allows OneDrive to automatically tag your photos by theme.
  • Notifications lets you get an email when people change files you’re sharing or when OneDrive recaps your photos.
  • Device backups shows a list of devices that are backing up settings to OneDrive.
  • Restore your OneDrive lets Microsoft 365 subscribers undo file and folder changes within the last 30 days. Files and folders created after the restore point are sent to the recycle bin. Before restoring, review the requirements and steps in Restore your OneDrive.
  • Search allows you to show previous searches as suggested search terms.

Store

How to access OneDrive settings in the OneDrive store app

  • Open the OneDrive Store app.

  • Select More (…).

  • Select Settings. Options include:

  • Reset app

  • Dark mode

  • Get more storage

Other OneDrive desktop options

These options apply to the OneDrive sync app on Windows and macOS.

  • Pause or resume syncing: Follow How to pause and resume OneDrive sync to choose a pause duration or resume syncing.
  • Close OneDrive: Select the OneDrive cloud icon in the Windows notification area or macOS menu bar, select Help & Settings (the gear icon ), and then select Close OneDrive. You can still access your files and folders online at onedrive.com.
  • Open the online recycle bin: Select the OneDrive cloud icon in the Windows notification area or macOS menu bar, and then select Recycle bin . For recovery steps, see Restore deleted files or folders in OneDrive.

Install OneDrive on an external drive

If you need to change your OneDrive storage location from your computer to an SD card or other external storage source, you can do so as long as the external drive is non-ejectable. Removable USB drives are not supported.

Note

If you don’t have enough room on your computer, use the Files On-Demand feature for OneDrive available for Windows and Mac, as well as selective syncing.

First, you should check the file system of the external drive you’ll be using.

Windows

Check the file system of the drive in Windows
  • Open File Explorer.
  • Right-click the drive and choose Properties.
  • On the General tab, next to File system, see if it says NTFS. If the file system is FAT or FAT32, refer to the next section. Otherwise, proceed to Unlink OneDrive and run OneDrive setup again.
Convert a FAT or FAT32 drive to NTFS

Converting a drive using these steps will preserve the files on the drive. We still recommend making sure you have backups of all files on the drive.

  • Find the letter of drive you want to convert. Open File Explorer, and in the left pane, look for the drive under “This PC” or “Computer.”
  • Press the Windows logo key + R to open the Run dialog box.
  • Enter cmd to open the command prompt window.
  • At the command line prompt, type convert drive: /fs:ntfs
  • For example, if the letter of the drive you want to convert is e, you would type convert e: /fs:ntfs Note

If you want to convert an NTFS drive back to FAT32, you need to save copies of any files you want to keep, and then reformat or partition the drive.

Unlink OneDrive and run OneDrive setup again in Windows

You won’t lose files or data by disabling, uninstalling or unlinking OneDrive on your computer. You can always access your files by signing in to your OneDrive account online.

  • Select the OneDrive cloud in your notification area to show the OneDrive pop-up.
  • Select the OneDrive Help and Settings icon then select Settings.
  • Go to the Account tab.
  • Select Unlink this PC, and then select Unlink account. Note

Unlinked files can be safely deleted from your local storage, as they are also stored in the cloud and accessible through the OneDrive site.

Follow the steps in the Welcome to OneDrive wizard to set up OneDrive in the new file location.

Warning

You cannot set up Folder Protection with OneDrive on external memory.

Reinstall OneDrive

Reinstalling Microsoft OneDrive can sometimes resolve sync issues and resets all OneDrive settings. OneDrive will perform a full sync after the reinstallation.

You won’t lose any data by uninstalling OneDrive. Your OneDrive folder will stop syncing, but any files or data you have in OneDrive will still be available when you sign in at OneDrive.com.

Windows

Reinstall OneDrive for Windows

The OneDrive app comes with some versions of Windows 10 and 11.

  • Select the Start button, type Programs in the search box, and then select Add or remove programs.
  • Under Apps & features find and select Microsoft OneDrive.
  • Note
    • Microsoft OneDrive is a backup and sync app, which is available for download from the OneDrive website.
    • OneDrive by Microsoft Corporation is an app available from the Microsoft Store app, which lets you view your OneDrive. You may have one or both apps installed (which is fine), but note the Store app does not backup and sync your files.
  • Select Uninstall. If you’re prompted for an administrator password or confirmation, type the password or provide confirmation.
  • If you need to backup and sync your files, download the Microsoft OneDrive app from the website.
  • Tip
  • If you only need to view your OneDrive, download the OneDrive app from the Microsoft Store. If you’re not sure which app you should install, read Which app do I need?
  • Open the downloaded file and follow the prompts to sign in and get started.
  • Note
    • If you had chosen to sync only some folders before the reset, you will need to do that again once sync has completed. Read Choose which OneDrive folders to sync to your computer for more information.
    • You will need to complete this for your OneDrive for work or school folders.

iPhone and iPad

To reinstall OneDrive for iOS

The best way to reset the app it to uninstall and reinstall it.

  • Uninstall the OneDrive app by pressing and holding the OneDrive app icon. Tap the ‘X’ in the corner and then accept the confirmation message to delete it.
  • Perform a “soft reset” by pressing and holding both the Sleep/Wake and Home buttons simultaneously for at least 10 seconds until you see the Apple logo. You can let go of both buttons after the Apple logo appears.
  • Reinstall the OneDrive app from the App Store.

Automatically save photos with OneDrive for Android and iOS

Use the OneDrive app for Android or iOS to automatically upload your camera roll. Choose your device’s tab for setup instructions.

Camera backup uploads photos and videos to OneDrive; it doesn’t sync them both ways. After photos and videos finish uploading, you can delete them from your device without affecting the copies in OneDrive.

Keep the OneDrive app running in the background. Closing the app can prevent automatic uploads.

iPhone and iPad

Upload your camera roll to OneDrive on iPhone or iPad

Important

You can upload your camera roll to only one account at a time. Make sure you’re signed in with the account you want to upload photos to. Tap the relevant account icon to switch accounts before turning on camera upload.

  • In the OneDrive app, tap your account image:
  • Tap Settings , then Camera Upload.
  • Turn on Camera Upload for the OneDrive account you want to upload photos to.
  • To ensure videos automatically upload, turn on Include Videos.
Use Bedtime Backup to upload remaining photos on iPhone or iPad

If you have large videos or need to upload lots of images, you might see some marked as Remaining. Use Bedtime Backup to upload your photos even faster with OneDrive’s dedicated upload mode. Here’s how:

Before you start, connect your iPhone or iPad to Wi-Fi and a charger.

  • Tap Remaining , and then tap Get Started.
  • Tap Turn on Bedtime Backup.
  • When uploads are complete, tap Turn Off Bedtime Backup.

Find your photos quickly with intelligent searches in OneDrive

Applies to: OneDrive.

If you want to find a photo—for example, of the first time a friend joined your annual camping trip in the mountains—the intelligent search in OneDrive can help you find it quickly. The search uses photo intelligence, locations, and more to find photos when you’re using OneDrive in a browser or on a mobile device.

To find your camping photo, you could search for “mountain camping” and look for the earliest photo of your friend in the search results. Or maybe you designed a conference booth for a company one year and you want to find those photos—you could search for something like “London conference booth.”

How to search photos in OneDrive using intelligent search

You can use intelligent searches when you’re using OneDrive in a browser or on a mobile device.

Search OneDrive photos using intelligent search in a web browser
  • In your browser, type photos.onedrive.com.
  • Start typing in the search bar at the top of the page. You can use words that describe a location or something visually distinctive. For example, “running in Sedona” or “outdoor wedding green dress.” OneDrive shows all the photos that match what you selected.

Note

Your feedback helps us ensure you have the best possible experiences with Microsoft. To give feedback, select on the search results page and tell us how we can improve our experience.

Search OneDrive photos using intelligent search on a mobile device
  • On your mobile device, open the OneDrive app.
  • Select Photos.
  • Select the search icon ( ) and start typing in the search bar at the top of the page. You can use words that describe a location or something visually distinctive. For example, “running in Sedona” or “outdoor wedding green dress.”
  • Select the Return or Go key. OneDrive shows all the photos that match what you selected.

Note

Your feedback helps us ensure you have the best possible experiences with Microsoft. To give feedback, select on the search results page and tell us how we can improve our experience.

Group photos by people in OneDrive

OneDrive can now use AI to recognize faces in your photos and group them together with facial grouping technology. Faces are grouped in the People section so you can view collections of photos based on people in it; and once you name the people, you can search for those photos faster.

Note

This feature is rolling out gradually and might not be available in your account or region yet. If you don’t see a People section in the OneDrive app, it hasn’t reached your account. When it does, the People section appears on its own - though some regions require your consent before we can begin processing your photos.

How facial grouping works in OneDrive Photos

Facial grouping uses AI technology to distinguish faces from other objects in an image and groups similar faces across photos by people.

Note

Groupings rely on the quality of your photos; groupings may not be entirely accurate.

Find people in your photos using OneDrive Photos

  • To find people in your photos, go to Photos > People in your OneDrive app. There may be a delay as we process your photos.
  • Note
  • Some regions require your consent before we can begin processing your photos.
  • When there are people ready to view, you can add names in the People section.
  • After naming people, you can easily search or filter by them.
  • Search:
  • Filter:
  • We will also provide recommendations of photos we think may belong to a person.

How OneDrive Photos collects and uses facial grouping data

Microsoft collects, uses, and stores facial scans and biometric information from your photos through the OneDrive app for facial grouping technologies. This helps you quickly and easily organize photos of friends and family. Only you can see your face groupings. If you share a photo or album with another individual, face groupings will not be shared.

Microsoft does not use any of your facial scans and biometric information to train or improve the AI model overall. Any data you provide is only used to help triage and improve the results of your account, no one else’s.

While the feature is on, Microsoft uses this data to group faces in your photos. You can turn this feature off at any time through Settings. When you turn off this feature in your OneDrive settings, all facial grouping data will be permanently removed within 30 days. Microsoft will further protect you by deleting your data after a period of inactivity. See the Microsoft account activity policy for more information.

For more information on our privacy policy, go to Microsoft Privacy Statement – Microsoft privacy.

Organize and find photos in OneDrive

After you upload photos , OneDrive helps you organize and find them. You can browse your memories fast with our new customizable Gallery, or find a photo based on where it was taken, what is in the photo, and whether it is a video, screenshot, document, and more!

Choose where you are looking at your photos.

Desktop

To help you find photos, the date appears over the scroll bar as you scroll up and down your photos:

Edit or remove photo tags in OneDrive on desktop

OneDrive automatically creates tags for things it recognizes. Sometimes it makes mistakes, but you can remove or edit the tags for a photo.

  • Hover your mouse over the photo to show the controls.
  • Select to open the info pane.
  • Type a new tag or select the X next to a tag to remove it. (You edit tags by adding or removing them.)
View all photos from the same location in OneDrive on desktop

If supported by the device taking them, photos have location tags, which you can use to quickly view all photos within the same location.

Caution

Location tags can reveal personal information so be careful when using them!

To find all photos within the same location, type the location in the search bar at the top of the screen. You may need to add the country too.

Tip

If search doesn’t find anything, but you know of at least one photo from that location, open the photo’s detailed information pane to see how Bing maps has recorded the location, and use that as your search term.

Create your own photo album in OneDrive on desktop

You can organize your photos into an album that you can share with friends or family.

  • Select the photos you want to add to the album and then click Add to album.
  • Either select New album and give it a name, or choose to add to one of your existing albums.

iPhone and iPad

To help you find photos, once you start scrolling, a month-find icon appears on the right to help you scroll faster.

Edit or remove photo tags in OneDrive on mobile

OneDrive automatically creates tags for things it recognizes. Sometimes it makes mistakes, but you can remove or edit the tags for a photo.

  • Open the photo and tap
  • Select Edit tags.
  • Type a new tag or tap the X next to a tag to remove it.
View all photos from the same location in OneDrive on mobile

If supported by the device taking them, photos have location tags, which you can use to quickly view all photos within the same location.

Caution

Location tags can reveal personal information so be careful when using them!

To find all photos within the same location, type the location in the search bar at the top of the screen. You may need to add the country too.

Tip

If search doesn’t find anything, but you know of at least one photo from that location, open the photo’s detailed information pane to see how Bing maps has recorded the location, and use that as your search term.

Create your own photo album in OneDrive on mobile

You can organize your photos into an album that you can share with friends or family.

  • Select the photos you want to add to the album and then tap
  • Either tap to create a new album, or choose to add to one of your existing albums in the list.

Scan a whiteboard, document, business card, or photo in OneDrive for iOS

You can scan whiteboards, business cards, or documents with the OneDrive app and automatically save them to your OneDrive for later use.

  • In the OneDrive app, tap Scan . You can also tap Add at the top of the screen, then tap Scan. (To exit out of Scan mode without scanning anything, just tap the left arrow icon in the upper left corner of your screen.)
  • Select the appropriate flash setting (on, off, automatic, or torch) by tapping the Flash icon in the upper right corner.
  • Select either Whiteboard, Document, Business Card, or Photo, then tap the white circle icon to scan the item. (On smaller screens, you may need to swipe left to see the Photo option.)
  • Tip
    • In iOS 11.31.5 and higher, you have the option for multi-page scanning, which helps you combine multiple scans into a single PDF. To use that option, tap Add, then scan your next document.
    • The maximum number of pages/images that can be multi-page scanned is 30.
  • Once you’ve scanned your item, you can crop it, rotate it, add text, or highlight part of it. (If you don’t like the image, tap the left arrow icon in the upper left to delete the scan and try again.)
  • You can also modify the filter you selected earlier (Whiteboard, Document, Business Card, or Photo), or change the mode (lighting adjustments and grayscale), by tapping Filters at the bottom.
  • Once you’re done editing your item, tap Done, enter a file name, then tap Save.
  • Note
  • Files are automatically saved as PDFs.

Seeing pictures that are not my photos in OneDrive

If you see pictures you don’t recognize in your OneDrive Memories or On This Day, it is because other apps’ folders are included in your device’s camera roll.

Examples of other folders included in your camera roll upload are social media apps, downloads and screenshots.

How to stop unrecognised photos from appearing in my OneDrive

Any pictures you see in OneDrive Memories or On this day are already included in your OneDrive. You can view the image details to see its filename and when the image was saved, or search for the filename online to see where it is stored.

If you don’t want to upload photos from folders other than your own camera roll, you can unselect them in the OneDrive mobile app.

  • Select Me
  • Open Settings
  • Select Camera upload
  • Choose Organise by source
  • Check or uncheck any folders you included or excluded.
  • Select Categorize in sub-folders to upload within the Pictures folder instead (e.g. Screenshots).

Share files and photos with family or Outlook groups

Note

Family and group sharing is included in all free and paid OneDrive for home (personal and family) plans on OneDrive for the web. This feature is not available for OneDrive for work or school accounts.

OneDrive makes it easier to stay connected with your family members, or groups that you’ve created in Outlook. Simply sign in to family.microsoft.com with your Microsoft account to predefine your family group, or create groups of people, such as friends, neighbors, or sports teams in Outlook. Then keep in touch easily by sharing photos, videos, and files with one click.

  • Predefine your family group by visiting family.microsoft.com. Or create a group of people, like a sports team, in Outlook.
  • Note
  • You’ll need to create a Microsoft family group to use this feature with your family members. Use a free Microsoft account, or the account associated with your Microsoft 365 Family, or Microsoft 365 Personal subscription to create your family group, then proceed to step 2.
  • Sign in with your Microsoft account at onedrive.com, and then browse to the location where you want to add the files.
  • Sign in​​​​​​​
  • Select My files or Photos on the left pane.
  • Pick the file or folder you want to share by selecting the circle in the upper corner of the item, then select Share at the top of the page.
  • Select Anyone with the link can edit if you want to customize access and edit permissions.
  • In the Enter a name or email address field, type Family or the name of your Outlook group, like Soccer team. When you type Family, OneDrive will give you the option to share with specific members by surfacing their names, or you can select Your family to share with your entire family.
  • Add a message and then send the invite.
  • To learn more about sharing files and photos in OneDrive and permission levels, see this article: Share OneDrive files and folders.

Sort, rename, or move photos and files in OneDrive

After you upload photos and files to OneDrive, you can sort, rearrange, rename, and move them on the OneDrive website to keep them organized. To see these options, sign in to OneDrive on the web with your personal Microsoft account.

Sort files in OneDrive

Note

As explained later in this article, the following steps don’t apply to Photo view, because this web-only view aggregates photos from various folder locations in OneDrive.

  • In OneDrive on the web, select My files and go to the folder that contains the files or photos you want to sort.
  • Select a column header, then select the display order you prefer. (For example, select the Name header, then select A to Z or Z to A.)
    • Alternately, select Sort at the upper right of the screen to specify the order your files are displayed in, such as by Name, Modified, or Sharing.
    • Note
    • The Sort option at the upper right is available only if you’re signed in with a Microsoft account.

Rename a file or folder in OneDrive

  • Select the file or folder you want to rename. (In List view, check the circle to the left of the item; in Tiles or Photo view, check the circle in the upper-right corner of the tile.)
  • Select Rename, and then enter a new name. Note

OneDrive can sometimes rename items with invalid characters for you.

Move a file or folder to a different location in OneDrive

To move a file or folder on OneDrive.com:

  • Browse to the file or folder that you want to move.

  • Select the item you want to move. (In List view, check the circle that appears to the left of the item when you hover the pointer there; in Tiles or Photo view, check the circle in the upper-right corner of the tile when you hover the pointer there.) You can also select multiple items to move them together, as a group.

  • In the top navigation, select Move to

  • In the Move to pane, browse to the destination folder, and then select Move.

  • If you want to create a new folder in which to store the item, select New folder.

  • If you need to move files or folders between OneDrive accounts (such as from a Microsoft account to a work or school account), you’ll have to sync the files to your PC or Mac and then use File Explorer (for Windows) or Mac Finder to move your files.

  • Note

  • You can’t move photos from Photo view because this web-only view aggregates photos from various folder locations in OneDrive. If you want to move the photos you see there, you’ll need to find the files in Files view (or in File Explorer or Finder) and then move the files from their actual locations. If you took the photos on a phone, try searching for the “Camera Roll” folder.

  • Similarly, you can’t move an album to another location, because an album is also an aggregated view of individual files, rather than a folder that’s easily moveable as a unit. Tip

  • If you’re signed in to the OneDrive desktop app on your computer, you can use File Explorer (or Mac Finder) to sort, move, and rename your OneDrive files and folders.

  • You can also use the OneDrive mobile app on your Android, iOS, or Windows device to sort, move, and rename files or folders.

Unable to access OneDrive from Insert Online Picture or Video

Applies to: OneDrive for Business 24, OneDrive for Business.

If you’re having trouble browsing your personal OneDrive for pictures or videos because of a limitation in Office, this article can help you fix the problem.

Regain access to pictures on your OneDrive

To add pictures from your personal OneDrive using Online Pictures in Office again, you need to update Office 2016.

There are two technologies for installing Office: Click-to-Run and Microsoft Installer (MSI). The type of installation you have will determine how you should update Office.

To determine whether you have a click-to-run or MSI version of Office by follow these steps:

  • Open any Office app.
  • Go to the File tab on the ribbon, select Account.
  • Look for the installation options.
  • Click-to-Run installations will have an Update Options button.
  • MSI-based installations don’t have an Update Options button. You’ll only see the About <application name> button. Select a heading for more information.
Update Click-to-Run installation of Office

If you have a Click-to-Run installation of Microsoft 365:

  • On the File > Account page, select Update Options, and then select Update Now.
  • Otherwise, Microsoft 365 updates immediately. After it’s done, open the File > Account page again and look at version number of Microsoft 365 that’s installed. You have successfully updated to a version that fixes the Online Pictures problem when your version number is at least:
  • Office 2016:
  • Channel
  • Minimum version number
  • Current Channel
  • 16.0.9001.2138
  • Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel (Preview)
  • 16.0.9001.2138
  • Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel
  • 16.0.8431.2137
  • If Update Now is grayed out, it means that your organization controls when you update to a new version of Microsoft 365. You’ll need to wait until your organization gets an update of Microsoft 365 to fix this online picture problem.
  • If you aren’t updated to an adequate version of Microsoft 365 yet, you can follow the steps in Insert video or picture files with the OneDrive app.
Update an MSI-based installation of Office

If you have an MSI-based installation of Microsoft 365, you or your administrator should first install the following patch:

  • Office 2016:KB4011632 After you have install the patch, you can add pictures again by using Online Pictures (as described in the article, Insert pictures).

If you haven’t installed the patch, you can follow the steps in Insert video or pictures files with OneDrive.

Insert video or picture files with the OneDrive app

You can add a video or picture from a personal OneDrive to a Office app. First, make sure the file is on your computer using the OneDrive desktop app.

  • If your PC is running Windows 10, the OneDrive app is already built-in to your system, and you’re ready to use the Insert tab as described in the following steps.
  • If you have a Mac, or if your PC is running an earlier version of Windows, go to https:⁠//onedrive.com/download to download the OneDrive app. After it is installed, you’re ready to use the Insert tab as described in the following steps. Note

The OneDrive app keeps a synchronized copy of all your OneDrive files on your computer. Watch a two-minute video to see how it works.

  • Open any Office app.
  • Go to the Insert tab of the ribbon. You have the following options:
    • For PowerPoint: Select Video > Video on My PC.
    • For all other apps: Select Pictures > This Device.
  • Select OneDrive – Personal from the location list on the left side of the dialog box.
  • Browse to the file you want to insert, select it, and then select Insert.

Insert a file you’ve downloaded from OneDrive.com

If you don’t want to have the OneDrive app installed on your computer, you can use the following steps to insert a OneDrive file into a Microsoft 365 app:

Download the file from OneDrive, then insert it

  • Go to https:⁠//onedrive.com and sign in with your Microsoft account.
  • Browse to the folder that contains your files and select the photo or video you want to insert.
  • Select Download and save the file to your computer.
  • In your app, select the Insert tab, then select Pictures or (on PowerPoint only) Video > Video on My PC. Then go to the location where you downloaded the file in step 3.
  • Select your file, and then select Insert.

Upload HEIF and HEVC photos and videos to OneDrive

OneDrive for iOS uploads High Efficiency Image File Format (HEIF) photos in their original format, instead of uploading them as JPG to OneDrive to preserve the image quality of original photos and to save storage space.

Note

Some iOS devices no longer have the option to save images as JPG.

How to view HEIF and HEVC photos and videos in OneDrive

If you’re using a non-Apple device (such as Android devices, PCs, or other Windows devices), you can preview HEIF and HEVC files in OneDrive and store them on your device, but you may not be able to open them without additional apps.

You can view your HEIF and HEVC files in the OneDrive website in any browser.

Change camera capture settings for HEIF and HEVC uploads to OneDrive

You may be able to update a setting on your Apple device camera to capture photos and videos in other formats.

  • On your iOS device, open Settings, then tap Camera > Format.
  • Under Camera Capture, tap Most Compatible.
  • Note
  • Some iOS devices no longer have the option to save images as Most Compatible.

How to open HEIF and HEVC files on Windows

You can view your HEIF and HEVC files in the OneDrive website in any browser.

To open and downloaded HEIF and HEVC files on your Windows computer, you may need to install a codec. Codecs are available from Microsoft and other third-party app developers.

Learn more

HEIF and High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) are the default file formats for photos and videos on most Apple devices running iOS 11 or later. Most Mac computers, iPhones, and iPads can open these files. You can also view these files on the OneDrive website.

To learn more about the HEIF and HEVC file format, and which Apple devices can capture media in HEIF or HEVC format, see using HEIF or HEVC media on Apple devices.

Upload photos and files to OneDrive

Applies to: OneDrive for Business.

You can add files to OneDrive in many different ways and then get to them from anywhere.

Using the OneDrive website

Depending on the web browser you use, you can upload files up to 250GB in size. (This limit is per file, not total.)

Note

For transferring large files or lots of files, we recommend adding the files to the OneDrive desktop app rather than using the Upload button on the website.

  • Sign in with your Microsoft account at onedrive.com, and then browse to the location where you want to add the files.

  • Sign in​​​​​​​

  • Select Upload.

  • Select the files you want to upload, and then select Open. Tip

  • You can also drag files from File Explorer or Mac Finder straight to your files on the OneDrive website.

  • In the Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge browser, you can also upload folders from the Folder option on the Upload menu or drag folders to the website.

  • Learn ways to organize and find photos in OneDrive.

Using File Explorer or Mac Finder to copy or move files to OneDrive

You can copy or move files between folders within OneDrive, or from other folders on your computer. (When you move files from other folders on your computer into a OneDrive folder, you’re removing them from your computer and adding them to OneDrive.)

For both File Explorer and Mac Finder, if you want to copy the item rather than move it, right-click the file or folder and select Copy, then open the OneDrive folder (or sub-folder) and right-click > Paste a copy of the item to OneDrive.

To move a file using Windows File Explorer, drag files from the file list in the right pane to OneDrive in the left pane.

To move a file using Mac Finder, drag files from the file list in the right pane to OneDrive in the left pane (if you have OneDrive listed there under Favorites). After a moment, Finder will switch to show your existing OneDrive files and folders in the right pane, and you can drag the file into the sub-folder of your choice.

In Windows 10 or 11

In new installations of Windows 10 or 11 for many eligible users, files save to OneDrive by default in Windows 10, rather than to your PC. This means you can access those files from any device that can connect to the Internet, and they are protected in case your computer is ever damaged. You can change your default save setting anytime. Learn how to set where your files are saved or move your files to OneDrive.

Saving to OneDrive automatically

You can save directly to OneDrive from Microsoft Office files (like Word docs and Excel worksheets), PDFs, and other documents. If your PC has a built-in camera, you can automatically save copies of the photos you take directly to OneDrive so you’ll always have a backup. To make sure your PC is set up to save automatically, check your OneDrive settings.

  • Swipe in from the right edge of the screen, tap Settings, and then tap Change PC settings. (If you’re using a mouse, point to the lower-right corner of the screen, move the mouse pointer up, click Settings, and then click Change PC settings.)
  • For documents, select OneDrive, and then turn on Save documents to OneDrive by default.
  • For photos, select Camera roll, and then choose Upload photos at good quality, or for higher resolution copies, choose Upload photos at best quality.
To move photos and files to OneDrive using the OneDrive app

When you move files, you’re removing them from your PC and adding them to OneDrive.

  • Select the arrow next to OneDrive and choose This PC.
  • Browse to the files you want to move, and then swipe down on them or right-click them to select them.
  • Select Cut.
  • Select the arrow next to This PC and choose OneDrive to browse to a folder in your OneDrive.
  • Swipe in from the top or bottom edge of the screen or right-click to open the app commands, and then select Paste.

Using the OneDrive desktop app

If you have a Mac, you can install the free OneDrive desktop app to upload files and folders to OneDrive automatically. Files you upload using the desktop app can be up to 20GB in size.

Using a mobile app

You can upload files to OneDrive using the OneDrive mobile app for Android or iOS. To learn how, see:

  • Upload files or photos to OneDrive in Android
  • Upload files or photos to OneDrive in iOS

From Microsoft Office or Microsoft 365

In any Office document, select File > Save As, choose your OneDrive, and then pick the folder where you want to save the file.

Note

  • Microsoft might limit the number of files that you can upload to OneDrive each month.
  • Respect copyright and be careful what you share online. Copying or sharing unauthorized materials violates the Microsoft Services Agreement.

Video formats you can play on Microsoft 365

Applies to: Microsoft Teams.

You can play most audio and video files directly from OneDrive, SharePoint, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft Clipchamp, Viva Engage, and all across Microsoft 365.

Supported audio and video file formats in Microsoft 365

The following audio/video files can be played directly from your Microsoft 365 in most browsers: 3G2, 3GP, 3GPP, ASF, AVI, M2TS, M4A, M4V, MKV, MOV, MP3, MP4, MP4V, MTS, TS, WAV, WEBM, WMA, WMV

Tip

For the best video playback experience, we recommend the following video encoding settings:

  • Container - MP4
  • Video - H.264 / MPEG-4 AVC, 30 fps, using these approximate bitrates based on resolution
    • ~8 Mbps or less for 1080p
    • ~5 Mbps or less for 720p
    • ~2.5 Mbps or less for 480p
    • ~1 Mbps or less for 360p or smaller
  • Audio - AAC, 384 Kbps or less If a file doesn’t play, the format might be one that either Microsoft 365 or your mobile device doesn’t support.

Note

DRM-protected video files can’t be played

How to add an embedded document or picture into a webpage

If you have a website or blog, it’s quick and easy to embed photos, Office documents, and other files from OneDrive. You can even customize how embedded Excel workbooks appear to other people.

  • Sign in to your account at onedrive.com.
  • Sign in
  • Go to OneDrive Files view and find the file you want to embed.
  • Select the file and click and select </> Embed.
  • Select Generate in the pane that opens to get the HTML needed for embedding your file. Important

Anyone who visits the webpage with this embedded file will be able to view it without signing in.

This item won’t load right now

If an embedded file no longer shows on your website or you see the error “This item won’t load right now”, it could be because the file is no longer available, or the link you used has changed.

To fix embedded files not showing:

  • Remove the original embedded HTML code from your website.
  • Sign in to your account at onedrive.com.
  • Sign in
  • Go to OneDrive Files view and find the file you want to embed.
  • Note
  • If the file you embedded is no longer shared with you, you cannot embed it.
  • Select the file and click and select </> Embed.
  • Select Generate in the pane that opens to get the HTML needed for re-embedding your file.
  • Important
  • Anyone who visits the webpage with this embedded file will be able to view it without signing in.

Restyle OneDrive images with AI

Note

Restyle with AI is only available to the Microsoft 365 Premium subscribers when using OneDrive for iOS, OneDrive for Android, or the OneDrive website.

What is Restyle with AI?

Restyle with AI is an AI-powered image editing system that you can use to transform the visual style of an existing photo by using natural language prompts or predefined styles.

Restyle with AI preserves the core elements of the original photo while it modifies attributes such as artistic style, lighting, color palette, textures, or mood.

Restyle with AI on OneDrive mobile apps:

Restyle with AI on the OneDrive website:

What are the intended uses of Restyle with AI?

Restyle with AI is designed for creative photo enhancement and experimentation. Intended uses include personal photo stylization, creative exploration, social sharing, and casual visual storytelling.

The system isn’t intended for identity alteration, sensitive attribute inference, or generating misleading or deceptive imagery. It’s also not designed for professional photo manipulation where precise, deterministic edits are required.

How to get the best results from Restyle with AI

Restyle with AI performs best on clear, well-lit images with recognizable subjects. Results might vary based on image resolution, lighting, and subject complexity.

Tip

  • Clearly specify desired styles or effects for improved results.
  • Review generated outputs carefully before sharing or publishing.
  • Avoid using AI Restyle for sensitive, confidential, or regulated content.
  • Respect copyright and intellectual property when uploading or transforming content. You can influence outcomes by choosing predefined styles, refining prompts, or selecting alternative generated results. Safety filters operate automatically and might block or modify certain requests to prevent harmful or sensitive outputs.

What are the limitations of Restyle with AI?

Restyle with AI might produce unexpected visual artifacts, partial prompt adherence, or stylistic over-application. It can struggle with complex scenes, small details, or ambiguous prompts. The system might also refuse certain prompts due to safety constraints.

You can minimize limitations by using clear, descriptive prompts, reviewing generated results before saving or sharing, and iterating with refined prompts. The original image always remains unchanged, so you can revert if needed.

Responsible AI - How was Restyle with AI evaluated?

Microsoft evaluated Restyle with AI using a combination of quantitative metrics and human review. Evaluation activities included prompt coverage testing, visual quality assessments, safety stress testing, and red teaming against prohibited or sensitive prompts.

Key metrics include image quality ratings, prompt adherence, visual artifact rate, safety violation rate, and user satisfaction signals. Results are most reliable for common consumer photo scenarios and might not generalize to niche artistic styles or extreme prompts that weren’t included in the evaluation.

How do I provide feedback on Restyle with AI?

You can provide feedback through in-product reporting mechanisms such as thumbs up or down, report issue actions, or feedback forms. The product team reviews feedback to improve quality, safety, and reliability.

Using Office Lens to adjust images in OneDrive

Office Lens is a great way to capture notes and info from whiteboards, menus, signs, handwritten memos, or anything with a lot of text. You don’t need to jot down notes, rely on blurry images or worry about misplacing anything. It’s great for capturing sketches, drawings and equations too, and even images without text.

Office Lens also gets rid of shadows and odd angles, so images are easier to read.

How to apply Office Lens correction to an image in OneDrive

  • Open your Photos in OneDrive.com.
  • Click to open the image you would like to adjust or clean up.
  • Note
  • You can only open one image at a time.
  • On the top menu, select Office Lens.
  • If you prefer the original image, simply select Revert to original.

How to undo automatic image correction in OneDrive

When reviewing your PC’s camera roll folder or photos in OneDrive, some images may appear to have been cropped or altered. This is because the Office Lens feature has detected the image to be from a whiteboard, menu or anything else with a lot of text and automatically made a more readable copy.

The original image is still safe and available, but you need to go to OneDrive.com to view it.

  • Open your Photos in OneDrive.com.
  • Click to open the image which has been cropped or altered.
  • Note
  • You can only open one image at a time.
  • On the top menu, select View original.
  • If you prefer the original image, select Revert to original.

Syncing and backup

Back up your folders with OneDrive

Applies to: OneDrive for Business 24, OneDrive for Business.

Every computer has standard folders such as Desktop, Documents, Music, Pictures, and Videos which you probably use but might not be included in your OneDrive. By backing up these folders to your OneDrive, they’re protected and available across all your devices.

Windows

Learn how to manage your OneDrive backup preferences. You’ll see which folders are currently backed up in OneDrive, and you can make changes on the spot:

Back up important Windows folders to OneDrive

Open OneDrive settings (select the OneDrive cloud icon in your notification area, and then select the OneDrive Help & Settings icon then Settings.)

  • Open OneDrive settings (select the OneDrive cloud icon in your notification area, and then select the OneDrive Help & Settings icon then Settings.)
  • Go to the Sync and backup tab.
  • Select Manage backup. To start backing up a folder, toggle any folder that says Not backed up, and then select Save changes.
Stop folder backup in OneDrive

To stop backing up a folder, select the toggle for the folder to turn it off.

  • Select the toggle for the folder to stop backup.
  • Choose whether to:
    • Keep the files only in OneDrive, removing them from your computer, or
    • Keep the files only on my PC, removing them from OneDrive. Note

If the folder you wish to stop backing up contains cloud only files, you will see a message saying “Some files couldn’t be moved. Download them first by changing their state to Always keep on this device”

Access your backed up folders on any device

When your files finish syncing to OneDrive, they’re backed up and you can access them from anywhere in Documents, or Desktop. When you back up your Desktop folder, the items on your desktop roam with you to your other desktops where you’re running OneDrive.

Buy or try Microsoft 365

If you’re signed in to the OneDrive sync app on your computer, you can use File Explorer to access your OneDrive. You can also use the OneDrive mobile app to access your folders on any device.

Fix problems with folder backup

Here are a list of errors you might see when you set up folder backup. Expand a section to see how to resolve them.

Folder backup not including Desktop & Documents in macOS

To enable back up of your important folders (Desktop, and Documents) in macOS, you need the following:

  • The standalone sync app, not the app from the Mac App Store. Uninstall any other versions of OneDrive then download the sync app.
  • Download
  • Your macOS device must have Full Disk Access enabled. Go to System Preferences > Security & Privacy Preferences > Privacy and add OneDrive to the list of applications. Change Privacy & Security settings on Mac. Tip

If you sign in with a work or school account, your IT Admin may have disabled this. IT Admins can configure device restriction settings in Microsoft Intune.

Folder protection is unavailable

A common reason for this error is that important folders on that are connected to a domain can’t be protected in a personal OneDrive account (when you’re signed in with a Microsoft account). For info about data protection solutions, contact your IT administrator. You shouldn’t have this issue with a work or school account.

File exceeds the maximum path length in Windows

Make sure the entire file path, including the file name, contains fewer than 260 characters. An example of a file path is:

C:&lt;UserName>\2017…

To resolve this, shorten the name of your file or the name of subfolders in OneDrive, or select a sub-folder that’s closer to the top-level folder.

File exceeds the maximum file size

OneDrive can’t sync files over 250GB. Remove these files from the folder you want to protect and then try again.

The file name isn’t allowed in OneDrive

File names can’t start with a space or include any of these characters:  : / * ? < > ” |. Move or rename the file to continue. Learn about OneDrive file naming restrictions.

The folder isn’t selected for syncing

The folder with the error is not syncing to your PC. To resolve this error, open OneDrive Settings (right-click the white or blue cloud icon in your notification area, and select Settings), select Choose Folders, and then make sure the folder you want to protect is selected. If Pictures is showing this error, make sure that Pictures, Screenshots, and Camera Roll are all selected (or don’t exist). It’s also possible that the OneDrive folder has a different name from the Windows important folder.

Important folders aren’t in the default locations

The folder with the error contains another important folder and can’t be protected until the contained folder is moved. Important folders that may be contained within the folder include: Documents, Desktop, Pictures, Screenshots, Camera Roll, or the OneDrive folder.

An unknown error occurred, with error code 0x80070005

If you receive error code 0x80070005, the “Prohibit User from manually redirecting Profile Folders” group policy is enabled. You may find that the files from the folders you selected were moved to identically named folders in your OneDrive folder, and the original locations are empty. Move the folder contents back to the original locations and ask your administrator whether the policy can be changed.

Folder contains a reparse point (junction point or symlink)

The folder you want to protect contains a special file type that links parts of the file system together. These items can’t be protected. To protect the folder, remove the file causing the issue.

Post PC folder backup

OneDrive tries to automatically re-open notebooks that were previously open. In rare cases, some notebooks may not be automatically loaded in the OneNote desktop app after PC folder backup. Workaround for this issue is to reopen the notebooks in the OneNote app using File > Open.

Caution

Some applications may depend on these links to function properly. Remove only the links that you know are safe to modify.

“File is open and cannot be moved” error

Any open files cannot be moved. Save and Close the file and try again.

“OneNote notebooks can’t be moved” error

If you try to stop back up for a folder that contains OneNote notebooks, you will see the “OneNote notebooks can’t be moved” error because Notebooks are cloud-based files and cannot be moved to your computer.

Browse and manage your photos on Windows

The updated Photos app on Windows 11 helps you browse, organize, and edit photos and videos from your PC, OneDrive, and iCloud. You can use Photos with pictures stored on your PC without signing in to OneDrive.

In Photos, you can:

  • Browse photos and videos from your PC, OneDrive, and iCloud in Gallery.
  • Search by what’s in your personal OneDrive photos, not only by file name. On a Copilot+ PC, search also covers indexed photos stored locally.
  • With a personal Microsoft account, find photos of friends or family in People, filter Gallery by people you name, revisit highlights in Moments, and create Albums.
  • Mark Favorites.
  • Crop and adjust photos with the updated editor.
  • Browse photos available on your device when you’re not connected to the internet.
  • Add local folders and use Windows actions with a photo: set it as your desktop background or lock screen, print it, or open it in File Explorer. With a work or school account, you can browse Gallery, search for a photo by file name or tags, mark Favorites, and add local folders. Albums, Moments, and People aren’t available for work or school accounts.

What’s changing on Windows 11

An updated Photos experience is rolling out on Windows 11, starting with Windows Insiders and expanding to other Windows 11 users later this year. The experience includes an updated gallery and editor.

When the updated experience is available on your device, Photos will have an updated icon. Follow the steps in View photos on Windows to open the app.

View photos on Windows

  • Select Start.
  • Enter Photos, and then open Photos. You don’t need to sign in to OneDrive to browse photos stored on your PC. Sign in with a personal Microsoft account or a work or school account to access your OneDrive photos.

You can also open Photos from the OneDrive activity center: select the OneDrive cloud icon in the notification area at the far right of the taskbar, then select View photos. This button is available when you’re signed in to OneDrive with a personal Microsoft account.

Choose which photos appear in the gallery

The Gallery shows photos from the sources you add in one timeline, with the newest photos first. These sources can include OneDrive and your PC. Your Pictures library appears automatically, including photos stored only on your PC.

To add another local folder stored on your PC:

  • Select This PC in the left navigation.
  • Select Add a folder, and then choose the folder you want to see. Note

Showing a folder in This PC doesn’t upload its photos to OneDrive. Photos stored in a folder synced with OneDrive are uploaded through OneDrive sync.

To narrow the photos currently shown, select Filter at the top of Gallery. You can filter by media type, favorites, source, orientation, and resolution. With a personal account, you can also filter by people you name.

If you want to choose which OneDrive folders appear in Gallery, or to hide screenshots and GIFs:

  • Select the Options button next to Filter.
  • Under Photos from OneDrive, select All OneDrive folders or Only the Pictures folder.
  • Under Declutter, select Hide screenshots and GIFs.
Include your iCloud photos

You can access all the media files on iCloud from the Photos app. Here’s how:

  • Select This PC in the left navigation.
  • Select iCloud Photos. You’re prompted to go to the Microsoft Store and download the iCloud for Windows app.
  • Open iCloud for Windows, sign in to your Apple Account, and then choose Photos in the iCloud app to view your iCloud media in the Photos app.
  • Open or go back to Photos. You can see all your iCloud content.

Search your photos

In Photos, select the search bar at the top. The search options depend on your account and device:

  • Personal OneDrive photos: Describe what you’re looking for, like “beach” or “birthday cake.” Search can find pictures by what’s in them, not just file names or dates.
  • Work or school OneDrive photos: Search by file name or tags.
  • Local photos on a Copilot+ PC: Describe what you’re looking for to search indexed photos stored on your PC. For supported languages, file types, and indexing requirements, see Search photos.

Turn off face grouping

The People feature is available for personal Microsoft accounts and groups photos of the same person so you can find their photos faster. Face grouping runs in the cloud and only on the photos in your OneDrive. Photos that are only on your PC aren’t processed.

Note

Face grouping is rolling out gradually and might not be available for your account or region yet. Some regions require your consent before photo processing can begin.

To turn off face grouping from the desktop app:

  • In Photos, select Settings.
  • Select More settings. OneDrive settings opens in your browser.
  • Select Photos, then turn off the setting in the People section. All face grouping data is permanently removed within 30 days.

To learn how face grouping works, how your data is used, and how to find and name people, see Group photos by people in OneDrive. To learn how Microsoft approaches AI features like this one, see Responsible AI.

Photos and OneDrive sync

OneDrive policies in Photos control access to OneDrive photos. You can still use Photos with pictures stored on your PC without signing in to OneDrive.

To stop OneDrive file sync on your device, see Turn off, disable, or uninstall OneDrive.

Manage photos on devices in your organization

Existing OneDrive policies apply to OneDrive functionality in Photos:

  • DisablePersonalSync prevents personal OneDrive account sign-in.
  • DisableNucleusSync prevents the use of any OneDrive account in Photos. These policies don’t prevent users from using Photos with local content.

For organizations using AppLocker packaged-app rules to block Microsoft Photos, update the rules to include Microsoft.OneDrive.Photos if you intend to continue blocking it.

If your organization disables Store-originated apps by using DisableStoreApps, the update won’t be installed on affected devices.

For most organizations, no new or immediate configuration is required. Review existing Windows app-management and OneDrive policies, especially rules that intentionally block or remove Photos.

For OneDrive policy guidance, see Use OneDrive policies to control sync settings.

Frequently asked questions

Is an updated Photos experience rolling out on Windows 11?

Yes. An updated Photos experience includes an updated gallery and editor. To open the experience available on your device, follow the steps in View photos on Windows.

Is the updated Photos experience rolling out to Windows Insiders first?

Yes. The updated experience is rolling out to Windows Insiders first, with availability expanding to other Windows 11 users later this year.

Do I need to sign in to use Photos?

No. You can browse pictures stored on your PC without signing in to OneDrive. Sign in with a personal Microsoft account or a work or school account to access your OneDrive photos.

Can I use Photos with a work or school account?

Yes. You can browse Gallery, search by file name or tags, mark Favorites, and add local folders. Albums, Moments, and People are available for personal accounts, not work or school accounts.

Does showing local photos in Photos upload them to OneDrive?

No. Showing photos stored on your PC in Photos doesn’t upload them. Photos stored in a folder synced with OneDrive are uploaded through OneDrive sync.

Does face grouping scan the photos on my PC?

No. Face grouping runs in the cloud and only on the photos in your OneDrive. Photos that are only on your PC aren’t processed for face grouping. For details, see Turn off face grouping.

Can I turn off face grouping?

Yes. Follow the steps in Turn off face grouping. All face grouping data is permanently removed within 30 days.

Changes to Samsung Gallery sync and OneDrive

Last updated: May 14, 2026

Overview

Starting September 30, 2026, Samsung Gallery will no longer sync directly with OneDrive.

After September 30, 2026, new users will not be able to link their Samsung Gallery and OneDrive apps.

If you previously used Samsung Gallery to OneDrive sync feature, you will need to update your camera roll settings to continue backing up new photos and videos and to access any photos you have already backed up via the OneDrive app.

Why use OneDrive for photo backup?

With OneDrive, your photos and videos are securely stored in the cloud, accessible across devices, automatically backed up, and easy to rediscover.

What’s changing in Samsung Gallery?

After September 30, 2026, Samsung Gallery will no longer sync photos to OneDrive. All photos stored in OneDrive will disappear from your Samsung Gallery app.

Note

Your OneDrive photos and videos are still accessible at onedrive.com or through all your devices where OneDrive is installed.

Use OneDrive to continue backing up, viewing, and managing your important photos and memories.

New photos and videos will only upload if:

  • OneDrive has permissions to access all your photos & videos.
  • Camera backup is turned on.

Who is affected by the changes?

  • Any OneDrive user on a Samsung device.
  • Anyone who has used Samsung Gallery sync to OneDrive.

What happens to my existing Samsung Gallery photos?

Your photos and videos already stored in OneDrive:

  • They remain safe and unchanged.
  • They continue to be accessible from all your devices where OneDrive is available.
  • They are not deleted or modified.

How do I keep backing up my photos to OneDrive?

To continue backing up your photos automatically:

  • Open the OneDrive app.
  • Log in with your Microsoft account if you are not already logged in. This may be different from your Samsung account.
  • Tap your Account Profile in the top left of the app.
  • Select Camera backup.
  • Ensure the correct account is selected.
  • Turn Camera backup on.
  • Grant access to photos and videos if prompted. Once enabled, new photos and videos will upload automatically. Learn more about how to Automatically save photos and videos with OneDrive.

Note

You must not exceed your storage quota. Learn about Microsoft storage quotas.

Why does OneDrive ask for permissions?

OneDrive requires access to your photos and videos to automatically back up new content. Make sure you give OneDrive access to all your photos and videos for backup to run properly in the background.

How much storage do I have?

If you need more space, you can upgrade your storage plan:

Explore OneDrive storage plans and upgrade options

Or manage your storage directly:

Clean up space on your Android device with OneDrive

Manage your OneDrive settings

You can review your camera backup settings, storage usage, and permissions in the OneDrive app or through your device’s OS settings.

Troubleshooting

If you don’t see new photos in OneDrive, check that Camera backup is turned on, your account is correct, you have storage availability, and strong internet connectivity.

For additional troubleshooting steps, see Troubleshoot OneDrive for Android app problems.

Choose which OneDrive folders you want to sync on Windows or macOS

Applies to: OneDrive for Business 24.

You can choose which OneDrive folders sync to your Windows or macOS device so you only keep important files available offline. This article explains how to manage folder selection in the OneDrive sync app and what happens when you stop syncing a folder.

Tip

When viewing your OneDrive via a web browser or mobile app, you will always see all your folders.

Windows

Steps to choose folders to sync in Windows

  • Open OneDrive settings (select the OneDrive cloud icon in your notification area, and then select the OneDrive Help and Settings icon then Settings.)

  • Go to the Account tab.

  • Select Choose folders.

  • In the Choose Folders dialog box, uncheck any folders you don’t want to sync to your computer and select OK. Note

  • You can only check or uncheck folders which are already included your OneDrive. Folders not in your OneDrive (such as external USB drive) cannot be included for sync. Learn how to upload photos and files to OneDrive.

  • You cannot uncheck certain folders which are important to the PC, including Documents, Desktop, Pictures and your Personal Vault folder.

  • If you uncheck a folder you are syncing to your computer, the folder will be removed from your computer, but the folder and its contents will still be available online.

  • Any custom sync settings you choose are unique to each computer, and each account.

Fix OneDrive Files On-Demand issues on macOS 12.1 or later

Applies to: OneDrive for Business.

On macOS 12.1 “Monterey” and later, macOS and OneDrive run a new Files On-Demand experience.

The macOS sync icons now look the same no matter which cloud service you use, and the macOS behavior might be new to you, so here are some useful tips:

Unable to turn off OneDrive files on-demand on macOS

From macOS 12.1, Files On Demand is part of macOS and cannot be turned off. You can still mark your files as Always Keep on This Device if you need them available when offline.

“Always Keep on This Device” not working in OneDrive on macOS

When you mark a file as “Always Keep on This Device” the cloud icon may remain. Below are the different conditions of an offline or online file or folder.

A locally available file or folder

This file or folder is always available. It was an online-only file which has been downloaded (rather than marked as “Always Keep on This Device”).

Online-only file or folder

This file or folder is only accessible when you are online and signed in to OneDrive.

Unopened offline cloud file or folder

This file or folder is always available. Both cloud and “Always available” icons are visible.

Opened offline cloud file or folder

This file or folder is always available and has been opened. Once opened, the cloud icon disappears.

OneDrive “Always Keep on This Device” files show zero bytes on macOS

If you see a difference between Size and Size on Disk when viewing file, folder or drive properties, read OneDrive disk space and file size don’t match.

AutoSave not working for OneDrive files on macOS

If you cannot find your files, read Missing files and autosave issues with OneDrive on macOS.

Fix “OneDrive couldn’t start” errors on macOS

If you’re upgrading to macOS 12.1 from an earlier version, OneDrive needs to migrate the Files On-Demand experience and will automatically do so for you.

If this process fails, you may get an error message. Below are examples of what that message might say, and how you can fix the problem.

OneDrive couldn’t start

Close and re-open OneDrive, then restart your computer.

An unknown error occurred with a system component. Please restart your Mac and try again.

This error means the migration failed because of a failure in a system component. Restart your Mac and try launching OneDrive again. If you still get the error, make sure you have updated to the latest macOS version.

OneDrive is running on an unsupported file system. Upgrade your file system to APFS and then restart OneDrive

This error is shown if you are running OneDrive on a file system other than Apple File System (APFS). Only APFS is supported in macOS 12.1 or later. You cannot run OneDrive on an HFS+.

Convert the file system that has OneDrive to APFS. You can use Disk Utility to perform this conversion. After you convert the file system, restart OneDrive.

Your OneDrive folder is locked or cannot be written. Ensure the folder is not locked and has appropriate permissions, and then restart OneDrive.

This error is shown if your OneDrive folder is locked, or you don’t have write permissions. Make sure the folder is unlocked and it is fully writable by you. Then restart OneDrive.

A system component blocked OneDrive from starting. Restart your Mac and try again.

This error means the migration failed because of a system component. Restart your Mac and try launching OneDrive again. If you still get the error, make sure you have updated the latest macOS version.

A required system component is unavailable on this version of macOS

This error is shown if you were previously using Files On-Demand and have upgraded to macOS 12.1, and the migration failed for a reason other than as described earlier in this document.

To correct this issue, you must reset your OneDrive.

Warning

Resetting your OneDrive will remove all local content. Anything that isn’t synced to the cloud may be lost.

To reset OneDrive:

  • Open Finder and navigate to the Applications folder.
  • Right-click on the OneDrive app and select Show Package Contents.
  • Go to Contents > Resources.
  • Double-click to run ResetOneDriveAppStandalone.command.
    • Depending on your OneDrive version, the command might be ResetOneDriveApp.command.
  • Launch OneDrive and set it up again.

  • Select the OneDrive Help and Settings icon then select Settings.
  • Go to the Account tab.
  • Select Unlink this PC, and then select Unlink account.
Clear sign in credentials in Windows
  • Press the Windows key + R to open a “Run” dialog.
  • Enter the path %localappdata%and select OK.
  • Delete the PreSignInSettingsConfig.json file.
Sign in again to re-link your account in Windows
  • Press the Windows key and type OneDrive.
  • Select the OneDrive app and sign in when prompted.
  • When you sign in, OneDrive will prompt you that a folder already exists: select Use this folder.
  • Tip
  • Select Choose new folder if you want to move your OneDrive to a new location.
  • OneDrive will now sync your files and folders back to your computer. OneDrive won’t download all your files (just their placeholders to save space; learn how Files On-Demand works), but this will still take some time.
  • Once your files have re-synced, you can clean up your Computer folder view and choose which folders to sync to your PC.
Still having problems?

Use our guided support troubleshooting tool or follow the steps in the sections below.

Start

Check that you can access your OneDrive for work or school account online
  • Sign in to Office 365 with your work or school account.
  • Now select the blue work or school OneDrive cloud icon in the notification area or menu bar.
  • Note
  • On a pc, you might need to click the Show hidden icons arrow next to the notification area to see the OneDrive icon, or click and start typing “select which icons” to display the notification area settings option, and then show Microsoft OneDrive. If the icon still doesn’t appear in the notification area, OneDrive might not be running. Click , type OneDrive in the search box, and then click OneDrive (not “OneDrive for work or school” as that may be an older version) in the search results.
  • Select View online If you cannot access your OneDrive for work or school online, contact your Network Administrator.
Update to the latest version of OneDrive

Note

Your IT admin may restrict what updates you are entitled to receive.

OneDrive and Windows are frequently updated and keeping your PC up to date can help sync problems.

  • Download the latest Windows updates or check for macOS updates to get the most out of OneDrive.
  • Download the latest version of OneDrive and install it.
  • Note
  • If you already have the latest version, the installer setup will end automatically. For more information on the latest version, read the release notes.
  • Press the Windows key and type OneDrive
  • Open the OneDrive app.
  • When OneDrive Setup starts, enter your work or school credentials, and then select Sign in to set up your account.
Move files out of a sync folder

If you see the sync icon stuck for a long period of time, moving some files out of a sync folder can help clear any sync issues.

  • Open OneDrive settings (select the OneDrive cloud icon in your notification area, and then select the OneDrive Help and Settings icon )

  • Select Pause syncing.

  • Choose how long you want to pause OneDrive. After choosing the time, perform the following:

  • Select a file from one of your sync folders and move it to a different folder that’s not part of OneDrive.

  • Select again and select Resume syncing…

  • Once sync is complete, move the file back again.

Use the Support and Recovery Assistant for Microsoft 365

The Support and Recovery Assistant app can help you identify and fix several issues with OneDrive for work or school sync. Read how to use the Office 365 Support and Recovery Assistant.

If your account or environment is not supported by the Support and Recovery Assistant, try these steps to get sync running on your PC.

Reset OneDrive

Resetting OneDrive can sometimes resolve sync issues. OneDrive will perform a full sync after the reset.

Note

  • Resetting OneDrive disconnects all your existing sync connections (including personal OneDrive and OneDrive for work or school if set up).
  • You won’t lose files or data by resetting OneDrive on your computer. Learn how to Reset OneDrive.

Fix paths that are too long to sync in OneDrive

Applies to: OneDrive for Windows.

When a path to a file or folder becomes too long for OneDrive Sync to handle, OneDrive pauses that item and keeps everything else syncing normally, then walks you through a quick fix so the paused item can sync again.

Note

A “path” is the complete address of a file. It includes every folder name in the chain plus the file name, all added together. A path can get too long because of one very long name or because a file is nested inside many folders. You do not need to delete anything to fix it, and you will not lose any of your content.

Example of a path

  • Windows (File Explorer) – work or school account
  • C:\Users\JaneDoe\OneDrive - Contoso\Projects\2026\Q1\Budget_Report_v3.xlsx
  • Windows (File Explorer) – personal account
  • C:\Users\JaneDoe\OneDrive\Projects\2026\Q1\Budget_Report_v3.xlsx

How you’ll know an item needs attention

When an item’s path is too long to sync, OneDrive lets you know with a red X:

  • Select the OneDrive cloud icon in the taskbar to open the Activity Center.
  • The item that needs attention is listed with a note that its path is too long to sync.
  • You’ll see two buttons next to it: Shorten path and Move file (or Move folder, depending on whether the item is a file or a folder).
  • Everything else keeps syncing. Only the listed item is paused.

How to fix “file or folder is too long” errors in OneDrive

You can fix a long path in either of two ways. Both get the item syncing again, so pick whichever is easier for you:

  • Shorten the path - rename the file, or one of the folders it sits inside, so the overall path is shorter.
  • Move the item - move the file or folder to a location in your OneDrive that isn’t nested as deeply. Your file stays in OneDrive either way, with its contents intact.
Option 1: Shorten the path by renaming it
  • In the OneDrive Activity Center, find the item that needs attention and select Shorten path.
  • The Shorten this path window opens. It shows the full path to your item as a list of folders, ending with the file or folder that’s too long.
  • At the bottom, OneDrive tells you how much shorter the path needs to be - for example, “Path is 32 characters too long.”
  • Select the file or a folder in the list and type a shorter name. The message at the bottom updates as you edit.
  • When the path is short enough, the message changes to “Path is short enough to sync” with a green checkmark.
  • Select Save changes to let OneDrive apply the new name and start syncing the item again. Note

Renaming a folder here renames it everywhere in your OneDrive, just like renaming it in File Explorer. Everything inside that folder stays with it.

Option 2: Shorten the path by moving the file to another location
  • In the Activity Center, select Move file (or Move folder) next to the item.
  • A File Explorer window opens that mentions at the top left corner how many characters are over limit.
  • Browse to a folder that’s closer to the top of your OneDrive (fewer folders deep).
  • Choose Select folder.
  • If you’re asked to confirm, review the message and select Move file (or Move folder) to let OneDrive move the item and resume syncing. Tip

Moving an item up even one or two folder levels is often enough to bring the path under the limit.

When more than one item needs fixing

Sometimes several files or folders have long paths at the same time. OneDrive groups them together in one list so you can work through them in one place.

  • Open the Activity Center and select Fix paths to open the Fix paths that are too long to sync list.
  • Each item shows by how many characters it is over. Point to an item, then select Shorten or Move to fix it - just as you would with a single item.
  • As you fix each one, it is cleared from the list.
  • Note
  • Fixing one folder can resolve several items at once. Because a folder’s name is part of the path for everything inside it, shortening or moving that folder often fixes the files beneath it automatically - so you may see several items clear from the list after a single change.

Files and folders you’ve shared with others

If the item you’re fixing is shared, OneDrive shows an extra confirmation before it makes the change.

  • Moving a shared item can change sharing permissions.
  • Review the message, then confirm to continue.

Files and folders in a shared library

Some items in your OneDrive are shortcuts to a shared folder. If a long-path item lives inside one of these shortcuts:

  • Fixing the path changes the item for everyone who uses that folder, not just you.
  • OneDrive shows a confirmation dialog explaining that the change affects the shared folder before anything happens.
  • If you’re not sure, check with the folder owner before you rename or move the item.

Tips to keep paths from getting too long

  • Keep folder names short and meaningful.
  • Avoid stacking many folders inside one another - flatter is better.
  • Watch out for very long file names, especially ones that repeat the folder name.
