Preserve your digital legacy with OneDrive

OneDrive Digital legacy is a way for you to leave your pictures and files with another person, so that they can access your OneDrive if you pass away or can’t use your account.

Important

Without OneDrive Digital legacy setup, Microsoft generally can’t provide your account information to non-account holders for privacy and other legal reasons. Learn more about your options.

How to give access to your OneDrive before your death

OneDrive Digital legacy allows you to grant read-only access to your next of kin, or a contact you trust to your OneDrive, so that in event of your death, they can view your files and photos.

Account holder actions

Trusted contact actions

1

Sign in to your OneDrive at onedrive.com and select Settings then Digital legacy.

Sign in.

2

Invite your trusted contact by entering their email and select Invite.

3

Open the “invitation to be their trusted contact for OneDrive”, select the link, and sign in using their credentials.

4

Go to Digital legacy and select Accept.

5

Go to Digital legacy and select Get code.

6

Share the code securely.

7

Go to Digital legacy and select Request access. Enter the code that has been shared or provided and wait 72 hours.

8

After 72 hours, access will be granted, and the button will change from Waiting to Go to files.

Note

  • Your trusted contact must have a Microsoft account. Create one.
  • If you send an invitation by mistake, or send it to the wrong person, select Cancel invitation.
  • You will be CC’d on the emails to your trusted contact, but you don’t need to respond.
  • You can share the Digital legacy code straight away, write it down in your Will, or give it to a third party such as lawyer or estate executor. The sharing code doesn’t change and doesn’t expire.
  • Digital legacy files are read only. Once files are downloaded, they can be modified or edited.

Digital legacy wasn’t set up, so how can someone access the user’s files?

We understand that these might be difficult times for those seeking access to someone’s email or storage accounts. If the user didn’t set up OneDrive Digital legacy, Microsoft generally can’t provide information to non-account holders for privacy and other legal reasons. Learn more about your options.

Report a concern in OneDrive

If you’ve received a link to an offensive or illegal file or folder stored in OneDrive, you can report it for us to review.

If you’re part of an organization that has its own procedures for reporting abuse, follow your organization’s procedures or start by contacting your Microsoft 365 administrator.

  • On the OneDrive website, sign in with your Microsoft account, and then check your Shared view.
  • If you don’t want to sign in or you want to report the file anonymously, use the anonymous Report Abuse form.
  • Right-click the offensive or illegal file and select Report a concern.
  • Select the reason you’re reporting the content, such as Suicide or self-harm, type any details you want to share in the comment box, and then select Report. Learn more about OneDrive personal digital safety policy and moderation process at OneDrive personal policy.

Note

If the offensive content was posted on a work or school account associated with a paid Microsoft 365 subscription, you will be directed to contact the organization responsible for the content directly.

Reset OneDrive

Applies to: OneDrive for Business 24, OneDrive for Business.

Resetting Microsoft OneDrive can sometimes resolve sync issues and resets all OneDrive settings. OneDrive will perform a full sync after the reset.

Important

You won’t lose files or data by resetting OneDrive on your computer. Resetting OneDrive only disconnects all your sync connections (including personal and work or school).

Windows

Follow the steps below to reset your OneDrive app

Step

Screenshot

1.⁠ On your computer keyboard, press the Windows key and R at the same time to open the Run dialog box.

2.⁠ Copy or type wsreset.exe into the box then select OK.

Note: A blank Command Prompt window will open and close briefly, then the Microsoft Store app will open. You can ignore these and close any unwanted windows.

If OneDrive is still not syncing, let’s continue with resetting the OneDrive sync app.

3.⁠ Press the Windows key and R again.

4.⁠ This time copy the text below and paste it into the dialog window, then press OK.

%localappdata%\Microsoft\OneDrive\onedrive.exe /reset

5.⁠ If you see a “Windows cannot find…” message, copy and paste the text below instead, then press OK.

C:\Program Files\Microsoft OneDrive\onedrive.exe /reset

6.⁠ If you still see a “Windows cannot find…” message, copy and paste the text below instead, then press OK.

C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft OneDrive\onedrive.exe /reset

Note: If none of these steps work, you do not have the OneDrive sync app installed. Find the right OneDrive app.

7.⁠ Manually restart OneDrive by going to Start , type OneDrive in the search box, and then click on the OneDrive desktop app.

Note

  • If none of these steps work, you do not have the OneDrive sync app installed. Find the right OneDrive app.
  • If you had chosen to sync only some folders before the reset, you will need to do that again once sync has completed. You will need to complete this for your personal OneDrive and OneDrive for work or school accounts. Read Choose which OneDrive folders to sync to your computer for more information.
To reset the OneDrive store app

Tip

If you’re not sure which OneDrive app you have, read Which OneDrive app do I have?

  • Press Start and enter apps:onedrive
  • Select App settings
  • Scroll down the list and select Reset.
What does resetting OneDrive do?

During a reset, OneDrive does the following:

  • Deletes the DAT file.
  • Stores the application logs in the registry.
  • Stores the settings on the disk. When OneDrive restarts, it checks with the registry to confirm the reset has taken place and then loads the settings and re-builds the DAT file.

You won’t lose any data by resetting OneDrive.

iPhone and iPad

To reset OneDrive on iOS

If you have issues with the app syncing your files or camera roll to OneDrive, you can reset it.

  • Go to Profile > Settings > Account (and if you have more than one set up, select the account to reset)

  • Select Reset. If you still have issues, uninstall and reinstall the app.

  • Uninstall the OneDrive app by pressing and holding the OneDrive app icon. Tap the ‘X’ in the corner and then accept the confirmation message to delete it.

  • Perform a “soft reset” by pressing and holding both the Sleep/Wake and Home buttons simultaneously for at least 10 seconds until you see the Apple logo. You can let go of both buttons after the Apple logo appears.

  • Reinstall the OneDrive app from the App Store.

Restrictions and limitations in OneDrive and SharePoint

Applies to: SharePoint in Microsoft 365, OneDrive for Windows.

This article describes the restrictions and limitations that apply to files, file names, and file types when you sync with OneDrive for home, OneDrive for work or school, or SharePoint in Microsoft 365.

Use the links in In this article to find the restriction or limit that matches your issue. Each section identifies the OneDrive account types it applies to. For SharePoint document libraries, also check the library-specific settings and limitations.

Note

For restrictions and limitations that apply to the earlier version of OneDrive for Business (groove.exe), SharePoint 2013, and SharePoint 2016, see KB 2933738.

What’s new

  • April 22, 2026: Started rollout of the public preview for syncing up to 1,000,000 items. Review the preview requirements and exclusions before using this limit.
  • January 28, 2025: OneDrive for Mac now supports invalid characters.

Restrictions

Invalid characters

Applies to: OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school.

Certain characters have special meanings when you use them in file names in OneDrive, SharePoint, Windows, and macOS. For example, “*” represents a wildcard, and “" appears in file name paths. If a file or folder you want to upload to OneDrive contains any of the characters in the following list, it might prevent files and folders from syncing. Rename the file or folder to remove these characters before you upload it.

The following characters aren’t allowed in file and folder names in OneDrive for home or OneDrive for work or school:

” * : < > ? /  |

Note

  • You can’t use leading and trailing spaces in file or folder names.
  • To rename a file or folder in Windows, select it and press F2. To rename a file or folder on a Mac, select it and press Return.
  • Some organizations don’t yet support ⁠#⁠ and ⁠%⁠ in names. If you’re a global admin or SharePoint admin in Microsoft 365, see Enabling # and % Support on the SharePoint blog to learn how to allow these characters.
  • For Office desktop Win32 apps: If you save an Office file through the Backstage view to a OneDrive or SharePoint folder, you can’t save the file if the folder name contains ⁠;⁠ (semicolon).
  • If you use Office 2010, you can’t use “⁠&⁠” in file and folder names.
  • For automatic renaming behavior, including changes from a comma to ^J, see Why has my filename changed?.
Invalid file or folder names

Applies to: OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school.

These names aren’t allowed for files or folders: .lock, CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM0 - COM9, LPT0 - LPT9, vti, desktop.ini, any filename starting with ⁠~$⁠.

Note

  • You can’t use vti anywhere in a file name.
  • You can’t use forms when the folder or file is at the root level of a library.
  • A folder name can’t start with either ゛ or ဧ.
Invalid or blocked file types

Applies to: OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school.

Temporary TMP files don’t sync to OneDrive. For more information, see OneDrive status stuck on “Sync pending”.

Files that your local computer uses, such as desktop.ini on Windows or .ds_store on macOS, don’t normally sync. If these files get uploaded to OneDrive during a migration, the sync app deletes the cloud copy and leaves the local copy.

Outlook .PST files are supported, but the sync app syncs them less frequently than other file types to reduce network traffic. To move .PST files out of OneDrive, see How to remove an Outlook PST data file from OneDrive.

For work or school accounts, admins can block syncing of specific file types. If Known Folder Move is enabled and configured through Group Policy, .PST files migrate. Outlook might show errors after migration because it’s still looking for the .PST files at their original location.

For OneDrive for work or school, your admin might prevent the sync app from uploading specific file types. Contact your admin if an organizational policy blocks a file you need to sync.

SharePoint in Microsoft 365 doesn’t have a general list of blocked file types. Some custom-script file types can be uploaded but won’t work unless the site allows custom script. For details and the separate restrictions for earlier SharePoint Server versions, see Types of files that cannot be added to a list or library.

Network or mapped drives

Applies to: OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school.

You can’t add a network or mapped drive as your OneDrive sync location. OneDrive doesn’t support syncing by using symbolic links or junction points.

Elevated privileges

Applies to: OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school.

OneDrive doesn’t support running with elevated privileges. When you run with elevated privileges, OneDrive menu items aren’t available in File Explorer. For troubleshooting, see Unable to share OneDrive files.

For multi-user computers or environments where executable files shouldn’t run from user profiles, admins can review per-machine sync app installation. A per-machine installation doesn’t change the restriction on running OneDrive with elevated privileges.

Sharing

Applies to: OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school.

You can’t share this item because the folder contains too many items

When you share a folder, you can include up to 50,000 sub-items within that folder and its subfolders.

To overcome this restriction, move some items into another folder that’s outside the original folder, or choose individual files to share.

You can’t break inheritance for this item because the list or library contains too many items with unique permissions

The supported limit for unique permissions in a list or library is 50,000 items. However, the recommended general limit is 5,000 items. Changing more than 5,000 uniquely permitted items at one time takes longer. For large lists, design the list to have as few unique permissions as possible.

Shared with me

You can’t synchronize the Shared with me view grouping of files from a OneDrive for work or school site.

Delivery failed to these recipients or groups error when sharing

You might receive this error message when you try to share to an address that isn’t associated with a Microsoft account.

How many OneDrive accounts?

Applies to: OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school.

Number of OneDrive accounts

You can sign in to and sync a limited number of accounts at the same time. Each device can have up to one OneDrive for home account and nine OneDrive for work or school accounts. For macOS devices, only one business account from the same organization can sync at a time.

OneDrive guest accounts

OneDrive supports syncing content as an external or guest user. For requirements, see B2B sync.

Authenticated proxies

Applies to: OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school.

OneDrive doesn’t support authenticated proxies.

If you see the error message “Your proxy settings require authentication” or the error code 0x8004de42 when you try to sign in to OneDrive, check that you’re not using an authenticated proxy to connect to OneDrive.

OneNote notebooks

Applies to: OneDrive for work or school.

OneNote notebooks have their own sync mechanism outside of OneDrive. If you plan on sharing a OneNote notebook—with yourself or others—it’s best to create it on OneDrive right from the start. Moving an existing OneNote notebook into a folder synced by OneDrive without going through the OneNote application isn’t currently supported.

Once a OneNote notebook is saved in OneDrive, if you are syncing the folder that contains the notebook, you find a stub .url file, which opens the notebook on the website.

OneNote notebooks saved in OneDrive or SharePoint are limited to 2 GB.

Read how to Move a OneNote notebook to OneDrive.

Virus detection

Applies to: OneDrive for work or school.

Microsoft 365 scans files uploaded to OneDrive and SharePoint and flags files when it detects malware. A file might sync to your computer before it’s marked as malware. After the file is marked, you can’t open the synced file locally.

You can check the status of files through the OneDrive web app. Infected files are marked with a red symbol beside the file name, indicating that the file is flagged as malware.

Important

Built-in virus detection isn’t a replacement for anti-malware protection on your devices. For details, see Built-in virus protection in SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft Teams.

Limitations

File upload and download sizes

Applies to: OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school.

Maximum

Upload

Download

Sync

250 GB

250 GB

Individual files

250 GB

250 GB

Files within a zip

250 GB

250 GB

Note

These limits apply to files, not your total storage. For any file larger than a few GB, use the OneDrive sync app instead of the website upload feature.

File name and path lengths

Applies to: OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school.

Different apps and Office versions have different limits. The combination of limitations might be unique to your setup.

For platform-specific limits and troubleshooting steps, see What are the file path length limits?.

Thumbnails and previews

Applies to: OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school.

The service doesn’t generate thumbnails for images larger than 100 MB.

The service doesn’t generate PDF previews for files larger than 100 MB.

Note

The service supports thumbnails only for OneDrive-supported file types, such as Office files, PDFs, and selected image and app types.

Number of items that can be synced or copied

Applies to: OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school.

Copy files on the OneDrive website

You can copy up to 2,500 files at one time on the OneDrive website.

Standard sync recommendation

For optimum performance outside the public preview described below, we recommend syncing no more than a total of 300,000 items across your cloud storage. Performance issues can occur if you have more than 300,000 items, even if you aren’t syncing all items.

Uploading, downloading, or moving many files at once can take a long time. During this time, the OneDrive desktop app status icon shows Syncing or Processing changes.

Public preview: sync up to 1,000,000 items

Support for syncing up to 1,000,000 items per sync instance per device is available in public preview for Windows and macOS. This preview doesn’t support virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) environments.

To participate in this preview, you must meet the following requirements:

  • Sync app: Use the latest OneDrive sync app with the OneDrive Insider program enabled. See How to access OneDrive settings.

  • Windows 11, Windows Server 2025, or macOS Golden Gate 27.

  • Memory: 8 GB RAM minimum (16 GB recommended).

  • Storage: Solid-state drive (SSD) required.

  • Processor: Intel i5 / AMD Ryzen 5 or later, Snapdragon X Plus or Apple silicon.

  • Recommended sync app configuration for Windows or macOS. Note

  • Devices that don’t meet these requirements continue to sync at the existing 300,000-item supported limit with no disruption.

  • Performance isn’t yet optimized for syncing a high volume of read-only files or for accounts under legal hold. Microsoft is actively working to improve performance and reliability for these scenarios.

  • Other SharePoint limits on viewing a document library on the web might affect how you structure your files in OneDrive.

Libraries with Information Rights Management enabled

Applies to: OneDrive for work or school.

To sync libraries as read/write, use the OneDrive sync app for Windows build 17.3.7294.0108 or later, or OneDrive for Mac build 18.151.0729.0014 or later.

Note

Admins: Learn how to configure the Azure Rights Management service.

Differential sync

Applies to: OneDrive for work or school.

Differential sync works for Microsoft Office files in the new file format, .docx, .pptx, and .xlsx.

This feature is part of Office integration and requires that you have:

  • Office 2016 Click-to-Run (version 16.0.6741.2027 or higher). You must also have OneDrive (version 17.3.6386.0412 or higher).
  • Office 2016 MSI and the following update installed: October 4, 2016, update for Office 2016 (KB3118262). You must also have OneDrive (version 17.3.6386.0412 or higher).
  • The Use Office applications to sync Office files setting turned on in the Office tab of OneDrive settings (PC) or OneDrive Preferences (Mac). For other file types, differential sync is available globally.

Note

OneNote files aren’t included. See OneNote notebooks.

Libraries with specific columns or metadata

Applies to: OneDrive for work or school.

If you have libraries with Checkout or Validation columns, or when Draft Item Security is set to either Only users who can edit or Only users who can approve items in Version Settings of the library:

  • For SharePoint document libraries, you synchronize these items as read-only.
  • For OneDrive libraries, OneDrive shows a lock icon ( ) next to the sync status and you can’t synchronize the library until you remove the settings.
Before you change library or site settings

These procedures are for people who have permission to manage the affected library or site. If you can’t access the settings, contact the library owner or your SharePoint admin.

Important

Changes to checkout, draft visibility, content approval, required columns, validation, or permissions affect everyone who uses the library or site. Confirm the changes with the owner before proceeding. Don’t remove controls that your organization requires just to enable syncing.

Open library settings

Use these steps whenever a procedure below directs you to open library settings:

  • Open the document library that you want to configure.
  • Select Settings > Library settings. In the classic experience, on the Library tab, in the Settings group, select Library Settings.
  • If a settings panel opens, select More library settings to open the full settings page. For versioning-related options, see Enable and configure versioning for a list or library.
Require Check Out
  • Open library settings.
  • Under General Settings, select Versioning settings.
  • Under Require Check Out, select No (default).
  • Select OK.
Draft Item Security
  • Open library settings.
  • Under General Settings, select Versioning settings.
  • Under Draft Item Security, select Any user who can read items (default).
  • Select OK.
Content Approval
  • Open library settings.
  • Under General Settings, select Versioning settings.
  • Under Content Approval, select No (default) for Require content approval for submitted items.
  • Select OK.
Required columns
  • Open library settings.
  • In the Columns section, review which columns are required. With the library owner’s approval, change the requirements so that no columns are required. Note

When you enable Management of content types, information about required columns might not be available. If you need to temporarily disable content type management to access the required-column settings, obtain the library owner’s approval first and re-enable it when you’re done.

Offline Client Availability at the library level
  • Open library settings.
  • Under General Settings, select Advanced settings.
  • Under Offline Client Availability, select Yes (default).
Offline Client Availability at the site level
  • Open the site that you want to configure.
  • In the classic toolbar, on the Site tab, in the Settings group, select Site Settings.
  • Under Search, select Search and offline availability.
  • Under Offline Client Availability, select Yes (default).
Limited-access user permission lockdown mode
  • Open Site Settings for the site that you want to configure.
  • Under Site Collection Administration, select Site collection features.
  • Find Limited-access user permission lockdown mode. If it’s enabled and the site owner approves the change, disable it and check whether syncing works.
Permissions
  • Open library settings.
  • Select Permissions for this document library, and then select Check Permissions for the user.
  • To sync the file in more than read-only mode, the user must have Contribute permissions or higher.
Validation
  • Open library settings.
  • Under General Settings, select Validation Settings.
  • Remove the validation that the library owner has approved for removal, and then select Save. After an approved change, check whether the affected files sync and whether the library or site still behaves as intended.

Learn more about how to manage Data and lists in SharePoint.

Windows-specific restrictions and limitations

Applies to: OneDrive for work or school.

File Explorer displays the first 35 characters of a site library’s name and site name combination for a library that you synchronize. This limitation doesn’t affect your ability to sync these items within the limits described in this article.

The sync app doesn’t support roaming, mandatory, and temporary Windows profiles. The OneDrive sync app supports only users who can write to OneDrive application directories.

The OneDrive sync app supports the following virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) configurations on supported operating systems:

  • Virtual desktops that persist between sessions.
  • Non-persistent virtual desktops that use Azure Virtual Desktop.
  • Non-persistent virtual desktops that use FSLogix Apps or FSLogix Office Container and a Microsoft 365 subscription. All non-persistent VDI environments require the latest version of FSLogix and a per-machine installation of the OneDrive sync app. Review the supported operating systems and configuration requirements in Use the sync app on virtual desktops. The 1,000,000-item public preview doesn’t support VDI environments.

For the sync app to work as designed, your environment must meet the following requirements:

  • The application is installed on the local computer.
  • The user can write to the user profile.
  • Data written to the user profile is saved to the local hard disk and is available without a network connection.
  • Folders don’t have the SetCaseSensitiveInfo setting enabled. For current operating system requirements, see OneDrive system requirements. For Files On-Demand setup, see the guidance for Windows or macOS.
macOS-specific restrictions and limitations

Applies to: OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school.

The sync app doesn’t support case-sensitive formatted disk volumes.

Note

The Invalid characters restrictions also apply to macOS.

Troubleshooting hints and tips

Follow these hints and tips to get the most out of OneDrive and to make sync as trouble-free as possible.

OneDrive system requirements

Applies to: OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school.

OneDrive requires an active Microsoft account or a work or school account. Your device must also meet operating system and file system requirements. See OneDrive system requirements.

Support and Recovery Assistant

Applies to: OneDrive for work or school.

Microsoft Support and Recovery Assistant has been replaced by troubleshooters integrated into Get Help. For the available troubleshooters, see Running troubleshooters in Get Help.

For OneDrive-specific troubleshooting, see Fix OneDrive for work or school sync problems.

Only sync what you need

Applies to: OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school.

OneDrive Files On-Demand helps you access your files without downloading all of them and using storage space on your device. See the guidance for Windows or macOS.

You can also download fewer files by choosing which OneDrive folders to sync to your computer.

Note

You don’t lose files or data by disabling or uninstalling OneDrive on your computer.

Check you’re not syncing too many files

Applies to: OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school.

If OneDrive sync seems stuck for a long time or the status shows “Processing 0KB of xMB”, you might have many files in OneDrive or many new files to upload. Review the standard sync recommendation and public preview requirements before deciding whether to reduce the number of items.

Note

For transferring large files or lots of files, add the files to the OneDrive desktop app rather than using the Upload button on the website.

To check the file and folder count for your local OneDrive folder on Windows:

  • Open File Explorer.
  • Right-click the OneDrive folder and select Properties.
  • Review the Contains field for the number of files and folders. This count describes the selected local folder, not all items across your cloud storage. If you aren’t participating in the public preview and exceed the 300,000-item recommendation, review how to cancel or stop sync in OneDrive and choose which OneDrive folders to sync.

If syncing is already in progress, try pausing and resuming OneDrive sync.

Make sure you don’t have duplicate filenames

Applies to: OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school.

You might have sync conflicts if you upload multiple files on the OneDrive website at the same time, or if you make changes in your OneDrive folder on another PC that syncs at the same time.

Sync issues can also occur if you edit files offline.

To reduce sync conflicts, rename the edited files or folders to something new or unique, and then save them again.

Samsung, Microsoft OneDrive, and your privacy

Applies to: Privacy, OneDrive.

On certain Samsung devices, you can now back up your Samsung Gallery photos and videos, and your MyFiles documents to OneDrive and use your Samsung account to sign in to your Microsoft account.

Important

As of May 1st, 2026, new users will no longer be able to link the Samsung Gallery app to Microsoft OneDrive. All existing Samsung Gallery and Microsoft OneDrive linked users should use OneDrive camera roll backup to ensure continued backup of their photos after September 30, 2026. Learn more about the changes to Samsung Gallery.

What data is shared between Samsung Gallery and Microsoft OneDrive, and how it is used

The following sections describe the data you’ll be sharing if you choose to connect your personal accounts from Microsoft and Samsung.

Shared from Samsung to Microsoft. When you connect accounts, you allow Samsung to provide Microsoft with the following data to be accessed, stored, and used in accordance with the Microsoft Privacy Statement:

  • Profile data—includes your Samsung unique identifier, which is used to help verify your identity.
  • Samsung Services data —includes the photos, videos, and files in your Samsung Services that you choose, which will allow you to selectively back up your Samsung Services data to OneDrive. Note that Samsung services include Gallery and MyFiles. The above data will be transferred to OneDrive servers located in the United States and other jurisdictions outside Korea. For more details, refer to the Samsung Privacy Policy.

Shared from Microsoft to Samsung. Connecting accounts means you also allow Microsoft to provide the following data to be accessed, stored, and used by Samsung in accordance with the Samsung Privacy Policy:

  • Profile data—includes your Microsoft account unique identifier, which is used to help verify your identity. Your profile photo and contact information will also be included, but Samsung will not store or use this data.
  • OneDrive data—includes your photos, videos, and files on your OneDrive, which will allow you to selectively back up your Samsung Services data to OneDrive.

How to disconnect your Samsung Gallery from OneDrive

If you want to stop the Samsung Gallery app syncing photos to OneDrive and remove the Samsung data sharing permissions to your Microsoft Account, you’ll need to edit how you sign-in to Microsoft:

  • Open your Microsoft Account’s Additional security options.
  • Next to Samsung account, select Remove.
  • On your mobile device, go to Settings > Accounts.
  • Scroll down and select your Samsung account.
  • Tap Apps and services then Connected services.
  • Remove your Microsoft account from the list of Linked accounts. Tip

You may also need to unlink your Microsoft account from your Samsung account Connected services.

Set up multi-factor authentication for Microsoft 365

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) helps you to access your accounts more securely. It’s a way to prove that you are who you say you are. Because passwords can be forgotten, stolen, or compromised, MFA is an additional security step that helps protect your account by making it harder for other people to sign in to your account.

Watch

Steps

When you sign in to your Microsoft 365 account a security dialog box appears reminding you to set up basic security:

  • In the Help us protect your account box, select Next.
  • If you don’t have the Microsoft Authenticator app for iOS, select Download now.
  • Tip
  • You can scan a QR code or send a link to your mobile device to download the Authenticator app from the Authenticator app page.
  • After you’ve downloaded Authenticator, select Next.
  • Select the phone method to receive codes by text.
  • When you receive a code by text, type code number into the box, and then select Next.
  • Select Next, and open Authenticator on your phone.
  • Scan the QR code on your screen with the Authenticator app, and then select Approve when you receive the phone notification.
  • Select Done.

Set up OneDrive included with Microsoft 365

OneDrive is your online cloud storage within Microsoft 365. It lets you store your individual work files that you don’t want your colleagues to have access to unless you choose to share the files with them. OneDrive is part of Windows, so it’s simple to make sure all of your computer files are saved to OneDrive, so you can access them from anywhere.

Sign into OneDrive

It’s simple to access OneDrive from any web browser. Just sign in with your Microsoft 365 account.

  • Go to microsoft365.com and sign in.
  • From the left navigation bar, select Apps.
  • In the app launcher, select OneDrive. Any files you’ve uploaded to OneDrive will already be there.

OneDrive basics

Navigation pane

  • Files is your home base where you can find all of your files and folders.

  • Recent shows the files you worked on last.

  • Shared are the files others have shared with you and the files you’ve shared with others.

  • Discover shows files that are trending around you from people you work with.

  • Recycle bin shows your deleted files and folders.

  • Shared libraries show files in recently visited Teams and SharePoint sites. Toolbar

  • Select New to create files or folders.

  • Select Upload to add files or folders to your OneDrive storage.

  • Select Sort to change how you’d like to view your files.

  • Select View to change the view.

  • Select Information to see details like who Has Access and Activity. Or, hover the cursor over a file and information will appear.

  • Use keywords and tags to Search for files or folders.

Upload files to OneDrive

  • Sign in to Office.com and go to OneDrive.
  • Select My Files.
  • Choose where you want to upload a file or folder.
  • Select Upload > Files or Folders.
  • Find what you want to upload and select Open.
  • Or, you can select files or folders on your computer and drag them into the OneDrive web browser window.

Set up OneDrive on your computer

When you have OneDrive set up on your computer, it can mean that the files on your computer are backed up to OneDrive, letting you access them from anywhere.

  • Select Start and search for OneDrive.
  • Sign in with your Microsoft 365 account.
  • Follow the prompts and finish the setup process. After you finish the setup process, your OneDrive folder will show in your File Explorer. It works a lot like any other folder on your computer. Add a folder or file and it automatically syncs to your OneDrive cloud storage.

OneDrive help & learning

Share an AI agent in OneDrive

Applies to: Microsoft 365 Business Premium, Microsoft 365 Business Standard.

You can share an AI agent with others just like you would share a file in OneDrive. Once shared, others can open the agent and ask questions about the files—but only if they also have permission to view the content inside.

Important

Upgrades are coming mid-November 2026 to agents in OneDrive. Learn more in Upgrade agents in OneDrive.

Note

AI agents are available with Microsoft Copilot for work or school accounts only.

Here’s how to share and what to know about access:

Share an AI agent file

  • Sign in to the OneDrive website with your work or school credentials.
  • Sign in
  • Find the .agent file you want to share.
  • Select the file, then choose Share from the toolbar or right-click menu.
  • Choose who you want to share with.
  • Select Send or Copy link.

Make sure others can access the content

Sharing the agent file does not automatically share the files inside it.

To make sure others can get answers from the agent:

  • Go to each file used by the agent
  • Share those files with the same people
  • Or save those files in a shared folder that everyone has access to Important

If someone opens the agent but doesn’t have access to the source files, they won’t get useful answers.

Stop sharing an AI agent

To stop sharing:

  • Select the .agent file.
  • Choose Manage access.
  • Remove people or change link settings.

Common sharing tips

  • Use shared folders when possible, to avoid manual permission updates
  • Update access if you add new files to the agent
  • Test the shared link with another account to confirm it works as expected

Unlink and re-link OneDrive

Applies to: OneDrive for Business 24, OneDrive for Business.

Unlinking and re-linking your computer to OneDrive can help solve some sync problems.

You can also use these same steps to move your OneDrive to a new location, such as an external disk drive.

Note

No data will be lost by unlinking and re-linking your OneDrive, your local folders are just disconnected from the cloud for a short while. Any changes made while you’re unlinked will be synced once re-linking is complete.

Windows

Unlink your OneDrive account in Windows (English content)
Steps to unlink your OneDrive account

  • Select the OneDrive cloud in your notification area to show the OneDrive pop-up.

  • Select the OneDrive Help and Settings icon then select Settings.

  • Go to the Account tab.

  • Select Unlink this PC, and then select Unlink account. Clear sign in credentials

  • Press the Windows key + R to open a “Run” dialog.

  • Enter the path %localappdata%and select OK.

  • Delete the PreSignInSettingsConfig.json file. Sign in again to re-link your account

  • Sign in when prompted.

  • Tip

  • If OneDrive doesn’t open, press the Windows key , type OneDrive then select the OneDrive app.

  • When you sign in, OneDrive will prompt you that a folder already exists: select Use this folder.

  • Tip

  • Select Choose new folder if you want to move your OneDrive to a new location.

  • OneDrive will now sync your files and folders back to your computer. OneDrive won’t download all your files (just their placeholders to save space; learn how Files On-Demand works), but this will still take some time.

  • Once your files have re-synced, you can clean up your Computer folder view and choose which folders to sync to your PC.

  • If you still have OneDrive sync issues, try resetting OneDrive.

Use OneDrive and M365 documents with your LMS

The Microsoft OneDrive Learning Tools Interoperability (LTI) App integrates with your LMS to bring Microsoft OneDrive and Microsoft Office 365 directly into your most important workflows.

Microsoft OneDrive LTI App allows you to:

  • Attach Office 365 files including Word documents, PowerPoint presentations, and Excel from the Rich Content Editor
  • Distribute Office 365 cloud assignments.
  • View and organize your personal and course Microsoft Office files.
  • Create collaborations where course members can work together on shared documents in real time.
  • Access multiple Microsoft OneDrive accounts, including personal and school accounts.
  • Integrate Office 365 files with your course modules.
  • Use your Microsoft account for single sign-on with your LMS. Important

If you have never used OneDrive and are accessing it within your LMS for the first time, OneDrive Picker will not appear nor display an error. To resolve this, visit https:⁠//onedrive.com/ and sign into your school account. After signing, you should be able to access the OneDrive Picker within your LMS.

Instructure canvas

Enable Microsoft OneDrive assignments

Educators can enable Microsoft OneDrive assignments to ensure that students are able to utilize Microsoft OneDrive within their courses.

Educators enabling OneDrive assignments
  • Go to the home page of your course.
  • Check for Microsoft OneDrive on the course navigation. Note

If you are able to see Microsoft OneDrive on the course navigation, then Microsoft OneDrive is already installed in your course (by admin or by you). If you cannot find Microsoft OneDrive in course settings, follow the steps below to configure Microsoft OneDrive into your course.

3⁠. Get the Client ID from your Canvas administrator.

4⁠. Go to the Settings section of your course navigation, select the Apps tab, and then select View App Configurations.

5⁠. Select +App.

6⁠. Select Configuration Type as By Client ID.

7⁠. Enter your Client ID and select Submit.

Note

Microsoft OneDrive will appear in the list of apps. If it doesn’t appear, refresh the browser page for it to appear.

Create a Microsoft OneDrive Cloud Assignment

Cloud assignments are templated assignments. All students get their own copy of the assignment and can edit their own copy. When students submit the assignment, their own copy gets submitted and is available to the educator in the speed grader for assessment.

Microsoft OneDrive allows you to use Office files (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) to provide assignment instructions to students or assignment templates for students to edit and submit.

Educators creating a OneDrive Cloud Assignment

1⁠. To include instructions about the assignment as an Office file within your assignment, select the Power Plug icon in the editor and select Microsoft OneDrive.

Note

For the first time, Microsoft OneDrive may not show up. In that case, you can choose View All and select Microsoft OneDrive from the popup.

2⁠. Select a file from the OneDrive file picker to embed or link the file.

Note

Files with .xls extensions cannot be embedded.

3⁠. To add a templated assignment, select External Tool as the Submission Type and select Find.

Note

After selecting Find, a popup should open.

4⁠. Select Microsoft OneDrive to open the OneDrive file picker.

5⁠. Select the file you want to serve as the templated assignment and select Attach.

Note

It will attach the file and show the popup again.

6⁠. Click or tap Select to confirm the selected file.

7⁠. Select other options for Submission Attempts and Assign, then Save or Save & Publish.

Important

After a Microsoft OneDrive cloud assignment is published, it should not be edited. If you edit it, a new document will be created and shared with students. If the students have attempted the previous assignment and you share a new assignment, the previous work of the students will be lost.

Students completing a OneDrive Cloud Assignment

A student will be able to edit and submit their own copy of an assignment.

1⁠. Locate the assignment and select Edit Document on toolbar.

Note

This opens the document in new tab. The Canvas tab shows a popup asking you to select the Refresh button once you are done editing the assignment in new tab.

2⁠. Close the tab where you are editing the assignment and go back to the Canvas tab.

Note

It is strongly encouraged that you close the tab after editing the assignment to ensure that all changes are successfully saved when you go back to Canvas tab to submit the assignment.

3⁠. Select Refresh on the popup.

4⁠. Check that all changes are visible and select Submit Assignment to submit your assignment.

Important

If you find that your changes are not reflected after selecting Refresh in Canvas, you should attempt the assignment again.

Create a Templateless Assignment

This type of assignment allows students to upload any file from their Microsoft OneDrive account to submit for the assignment. Students are only able to upload Word, Excel and PowerPoint files.

Educators creating a templateless assignment
  • Create a new assignment.
  • Add assignment instructions.
  • Select Online for the submission type. 4⁠. Select the File Uploads box.

5⁠. Select other options for Submission Attempts and Assign, then Save or Save & Publish.

Students completing a templateless assignment
  • Go to the assignment and select Start Assignment.
  • Select Microsoft OneDrive tab, choose a file, and select Submit. 3⁠. Select Submit Assignment to submit your assignment.

Note

Submitted assignments can be accessed on top right of the page.

Collaborate using Microsoft OneDrive

Collaborations allow students to work collaboratively on a given document. Students and educators can start a collaboration. The document under collaboration remains accessible to educators even if the educator is not added to the collaboration.

Educators collaborating with OneDrive
  • To start the collaboration, select Microsoft OneDrive from the dropdown.
  • Choose your Type, Document type, and insert Description.
  • Tap or click Select Existing Document. Note

This opens OneDrive file picker.

4⁠. Select the file to collaborate on and click or tap Select.

5⁠. Assign the collaboration to students and select Save.

Note

  • This creates the collaboration for selected users, including the educator.
  • If you are using private mode of Safari browser, you will not be able to assign a collaboration to a group of students.
  • If you are using Firefox browser, a dialog box will appear asking you to Resend or Cancel. You will need to Cancel to create the collaboration.
Students collaborating with OneDrive
  • Select Collaborations from the course navigation.

This opens the collaboration document in new tab where you can see other students editing the same document.

Using Samsung Gallery with OneDrive

Important

Starting September 30, 2026, Samsung Gallery will no longer sync directly with Microsoft OneDrive. New users will not be able to link their Samsung Gallery and OneDrive accounts. All existing Samsung Gallery and Microsoft OneDrive linked users should use OneDrive camera roll backup to ensure continued backup and access to their photos. Learn more about the changes to Samsung Gallery.

To connect your Samsung Gallery to Microsoft OneDrive

  • Open the Gallery app settings.

  • Tap Sync to OneDrive and follow the prompts to sync your Samsung Cloud Gallery to Microsoft OneDrive. Note

  • Samsung Gallery connection to OneDrive is available for certain carriers, models, and markets only.

  • Your Samsung Gallery can only be connected to OneDrive personal accounts (i.e., not OneDrive for work or school users).

  • Switching to Samsung Gallery will again upload all your photos that were already uploaded to OneDrive by Camera Upload. Similarly, if you switch from Samsung Gallery to OneDrive Camera Upload, then all your permissible photos will get uploaded on the device.

Troubleshooting Samsung Gallery upload issues with OneDrive

  • If you connected your Samsung Gallery app to OneDrive, and see the error message “Something went wrong”, close the app and start the connection again, ensuring that all permissions are granted.
  • Note
    • Your Samsung Gallery can only be connected to OneDrive personal accounts (i.e., not OneDrive for work or school users).
    • If the Samsung Gallery still doesn’t sync to your OneDrive, contact Samsung Customer Support via your device. Go to Settings > Accounts and backup > Samsung Cloud > More options > Settings > Contact us > Error reports ensuring that Send system log data is enabled.
    • Any files larger than 4 GB cannot be uploaded automatically, but you can upload them manually.
  • If you connected your Samsung Gallery app to OneDrive, but images from other folders (e.g. Screenshots, social media folders) are not showing in your OneDrive camera roll, try the following solutions to solve this:
    • Disconnect your Samsung Gallery from OneDrive - see below.
    • Ensure that Gallery sync with OneDrive is enabled. Learn how to Automatically save photos and videos with OneDrive for Android.
    • Go to Settings > Accounts and backup > Samsung Cloud > Gallery > Albums to sync and select either All albums or choose the folders you’d like to sync. Note

Once photos and videos from the albums are synced, they’ll stay saved on OneDrive even if you stop syncing the albums or stop syncing with OneDrive.

Troubleshooting missing photos in Samsung Gallery

If you delete files from the Samsung Gallery folder in your OneDrive app or from within the Samsung Gallery app, they will be deleted from the other app too.

Warning

  • If you delete any files that sync to the Samsung Gallery, they will be moved to the Recycle Bin and deleted from all your synced devices.
  • Samsung Gallery is a bi-directional sync; files modified or deleted from the Samsung Gallery will be reflected on the cloud. Any modifications or deletions done on the web or from other OneDrive endpoints will delete your data on the device.

To disconnect your Samsung Gallery from OneDrive

If you want to stop the Samsung Gallery app from syncing photos to OneDrive and remove the Samsung data sharing permissions from your Microsoft account, you’ll need to edit how you sign in to Microsoft:

  • Open your Microsoft account’s Additional security options.
    • Next to Samsung Cloud, select Remove these permissions.
  • On your mobile device, go to Settings > Accounts and backup > Manage accounts.
    • Scroll down and select your Samsung account.
    • Go to Apps and services > Linked accounts >My profile > Linked accounts.
    • Unlink your Microsoft account from the list of Linked accounts.

Frequently asked questions on Samsung OneDrive bonus

I want to increase the storage space during the period. How much will I need to pay?

There are a number of options to purchase more storage. You can find the various plans and prices from the Plans and upgrades page of your OneDrive account, [or the app].

Can I add Samsung offers to other OneDrive storage offers?

Yes. Each storage offer is separate and offers may overlap.

Do existing Microsoft account users receive the same benefit as new users?

Yes, but note that each Microsoft account holder can only redeem a Bonus once.

Expiring offers

I want to keep the extra storage after the offer period. How much will I need to pay?

There are several options to purchase more storage. You can find the various plans and prices from the Plans and upgrades page of your OneDrive account.

What will happen to the files that are stored in OneDrive when the additional storage expires?

After two years, you can still access and download all your files in OneDrive, but your OneDrive account will be frozen if you exceed your OneDrive storage limit for more than three months. You can purchase additional storage if your OneDrive account exceeds the 5GB of storage that all users get for free. Read more about when your OneDrive account is frozen.

Is there any notification when the bonus offer will expire?

Yes. Before the bonus expires, you will see a notification.

Replacement devices

If I sell, damage or lose my device, does the Samsung offer continue?

Yes, the extra storage continues on your Microsoft account for the remaining term of the offer.

What happens if I had a bonus on my old phone and I buy a new device?

The storage continues on your Microsoft account for the remaining term of the offer on your old phone. It cannot be extended by buying a new device because each Microsoft account holder can only redeem a Bonus once.

What happens if I buy a second-hand device?

The OneDrive offer can only be redeemed once per device. Second-hand devices are only eligible if OneDrive was pre-installed and the previous owner did not redeem the offer and you have not taken out an offer previously.

What happens if I buy an additional Samsung device?

Each Microsoft account holder can only redeem a Samsung Bonus once. If you purchase another device, you will not get an additional offer.

What is OneDrive for work or school?

Applies to: Office 365 Small Business, Microsoft 365 admin.

OneDrive is the Microsoft cloud service that connects you to all your files. It lets you store and protect your files, share them with others, and access them from any of your devices. When you use OneDrive with an account provided by your company or school, it’s sometimes called “OneDrive for work or school.” It used to be known as “OneDrive for Business,” so you may still see it called that in places.

Store your work or school documents and related files

If you’re using Microsoft 365, you get at least 1 TB of space in the cloud, depending on your plan. If your OneDrive library is hosted on SharePoint Server in your organization, your organization’s administrators determine how much storage space is available.

All files that you store in OneDrive are private unless you decide to share them. You can share files and folders with co-workers so you can collaborate on projects. If you’re signed in to Microsoft 365, you may be able to share files with partners outside your organization, depending on what your company allows.

Tip

When you send email from Outlook Web App, you can attach a link to a OneDrive file instead of sending the file as an attachment. When you attach a file as a link, the people who receive the message automatically get permission to edit the file. This saves space in everyone’s mailbox and encourages people to edit the same copy in OneDrive.

To get to OneDrive:

  • Sign in to Microsoft 365 or your SharePoint site with your work or school account.
  • At the top of the page, select the app launcher , and then select OneDrive. OneDrive is part of your organization’s SharePoint environment, either in Microsoft 365 or in an on-premises installation of SharePoint Server.

Sync OneDrive to your computer

Use the OneDrive sync app to sync OneDrive with your computer. Learn how to sync files in Windows or sync files on a Mac. If the sync app isn’t installed, download OneDrive.

How is OneDrive for work or school different from OneDrive for home?

You can use the same apps to sync files to your Windows PC or Mac, or access them from your Android or iOS device. Sign in with your work or school account to use OneDrive for work or school, or sign in with your Microsoft account to use OneDrive for home.

  • OneDrive for home is online personal storage that you get when you set up a Microsoft account to use services such as Outlook.com or Xbox. Use OneDrive to save documents, photos, and other files in the cloud, share them with friends, and even collaborate on content. When you subscribe to Microsoft 365, you get 1 TB of storage and premium OneDrive features.
  • OneDrive for work or school is online storage for your work or school organization. Your organization manages this OneDrive, which lets you share work documents and collaborate on them with co-workers or classmates. Site collection administrators in your organization control what you can do in your OneDrive library. Although you can’t connect your OneDrive for home to your Microsoft 365 business account, you can copy or move files between the two OneDrive accounts. To move files between your personal OneDrive and your work or school OneDrive, follow these steps:
Copy files between OneDrive for home and OneDrive for work or school
  • Sync both versions of OneDrive to your local computer. See Sync files with OneDrive in Windows for more info.
  • Open both folders on your computer and copy or drag files from one folder to the other.
  • Sync both folders with OneDrive again.

Which app do i have

Sometimes, it can be handy to know which version and build of OneDrive you have so you can check on fixes and features in your release.

Choose your operating system to see which version of OneDrive you are using.

Windows 10/11

Press Start > Settings > Apps and search for “OneDrive”:

Microsoft OneDrive is a backup and sync app, which is available for download from the OneDrive website.

OneDrive by Microsoft Corporation is an app available from the Microsoft Store app, which lets you view your OneDrive.

You may have one or both apps installed (which is fine), but note the Store app does not backup and sync your files. If you need to backup and sync your files, download the Microsoft OneDrive app from the website.

Microsoft OneDrive

  • Open OneDrive settings (select the OneDrive cloud icon in your notification area, and then select the OneDrive Help and Settings icon then Settings.)
  • Go to the About tab to see the version number.
  • Tip
  • Check the box to access to pre-release versions of OneDrive on your computer. Click the Version number link or read the OneDrive Release Notes for more information on fixes and features in your release. (The latest version is Version 24.161.0811.0001 (August 21, 2024).)

OneDrive by Microsoft Corporation

  • Open the app and click Settings > About to read the version number.
Mac
  • Click the OneDrive cloud icon up in your Menu bar, click the three dots to open the menu, and select Preferences.
  • Go to the About tab to see the version number.
  • Tip
  • Check the box to access to pre-release versions of OneDrive on your computer. Read the OneDrive Release Notes for more information on fixes and features in your release. (The latest version is Version 24.161.0811.0001 (August 21, 2024).)
Android

Open the OneDrive app and select Me > Settings > About

Read the OneDrive Release Notes and more information on fixes and features in your release. (The latest version is v6.81 (1 Jun 2023).)

Join the OneDrive Preview for Android and get early access to new features in the OneDrive Android app.

iOS

Open the OneDrive app and select Me > Settings > Version

Read the OneDrive Release Notes and more information on fixes and features in your release. (The latest version is v14.8.3 (30 May 2023).)

Join the OneDrive Preview for iOS and get early access to new features in the OneDrive iOS app.

Why am I receiving email notifications from OneDrive?

As work becomes more collaborative and distributed, it can be hard to keep track of changes in documents. To help manage changes in documents saved to OneDrive or OneDrive mobile, OneDrive will notify you when comments are added to a document you created or when someone replied to a comment you made. These notifications are designed to draw your attention to important changes in a document and make it easier to stay aware of these changes.

Why are some OneDrive email notifications grouped into a single message while others aren’t?

To reduce the number of emails sent, we group notifications received in documents that have a lot of recent activity.

How do I give feedback on OneDrive email notifications?

We’d love to hear about your experience with notifications in OneDrive. Use the comments section below to share any ideas or feedback. To leave a comment, choose “Yes” or “No” next to “Was this information helpful,” enter your feedback, and then select Send.
